emissionParagraphs.text: An agentic system is a coupled decision process whose behavior depends on a predictive model and on the machinery that determines what the model observes, which actions can execute, what persists, and how success is established. Treating the model endpoint as the whole system hides variables that can dominate an experiment. A model that proposes a valid shell command has not thereby completed a repository repair. The command must execute in the intended checkout, its effects must survive interruption, the resulting program must satisfy the specification, and the evidence must reach a decision maker. Each transition introduces an independently testable mechanism.
Let the operational configuration be

where is the model, the tokenizer and serialization interface, the decoding configuration, the context constructor, the persistent-state update rule, the tool interface, the execution runtime, a collection of validators, and the authorization mechanism. None of these components is assumed correct. The environment supplies observations and receives effects. A complete trajectory includes attempted actions, rejected actions, tool errors, state mutations, validator outputs, and termination, rather than only model messages. This boundary permits scientific attribution: changing a model and changing a harness are different interventions even if both increase a benchmark score.

The term agentic identifies controlled interaction, not a particular software package or level of intelligence. A fixed workflow can invoke a powerful model without delegating its control flow. Conversely, a modest model can choose among tools and adapt a plan, while remaining severely limited in competence. Useful architectural descriptions therefore state which decisions are model-controlled, which are deterministic, and which require external authority. The ReAct formulation connects reasoning and environment actions, while SWE-agent demonstrates that the interaction interface around a model is itself an important engineering object. Neither establishes that every autonomous loop has useful generality .

Three boundaries are especially consequential. The epistemic boundary separates available observations from latent environment state. The authority boundary separates a plausible model proposal from an executable permission. The commit boundary separates an attempted operation from an effect that has become durable or externally visible. A retrieved document may cross the epistemic boundary without crossing the authority boundary: observing an instruction does not grant permission to obey it. A tool response may report success without crossing a verified commit boundary: the operation may have been accepted asynchronously and later failed. Reliable autonomy requires all three boundaries to be represented explicitly.

This perspective explains why the ecosystem cannot be reduced to a list of models or SDK names. Tokenizers determine representational interfaces; context managers select current evidence; sessions preserve continuity; memory services retain and reinterpret information; skills package procedures; protocols transport capabilities and results; runtimes mediate side effects; evaluators define what is counted as success. Their interactions, rather than their isolated presence, are the main technical subject of this book.

October 2026 evidence makes this boundary experimentally consequential. TraceTrial-Bench separates task outcomes from harness-criterion satisfaction, using native traces and environment evidence rather than treating a successful deliverable as proof that every runtime obligation held . ASAP evaluates frozen pretrained models through completion-based trajectory continuation, with reference prefixes and bounded recovery interventions . Its observed competence therefore belongs to that elicitation protocol, not to an unaided model in an unspecified interface. These studies motivate recording both the system under test and the apparatus that measures it; neither a benchmark name nor a model name uniquely identifies the experiment.

Let be the ordered interaction records available at decision time . History is not necessarily complete: a logging failure can omit an externally visible effect. Let denote persistent memory, the working context, the environment state, and the versioned compatibility manifest. Current authority is indexed separately by epoch . The trusted observation map reads authorization-relevant state; it need not reveal that privileged information to the model. With resource budget , an agent step factors as

The decision gates dispatch; denial does not prevent unrelated actors from changing . The locator binds the actual model input and decoding configuration to retained evidence. A locator or digest alone does not recover unavailable content. The partial journal operator returns the acknowledged append or the unresolved marker ; the displayed memory update is defined only on its successful branch. An effect may precede a failed journal write, so recovery must reconcile it before claiming continuity. Current authority must remain valid at dispatch under the service’s concurrency contract. Neither the notation nor a local append establishes an atomic transaction with an external service.

The parameters and component implementations in are fixed within the stated comparison epoch. Persistent-memory updates occur through ; changing model weights, prompt templates, executable skill implementations, or harness code changes the versioned configuration and requires an explicit outer transition. This distinction prevents a purported memory ablation from silently becoming a policy or runtime rewrite. Compatibility metadata and authority have different clocks: a restored model manifest cannot restore an expired external grant.

Editing a working context or selecting an already versioned skill can remain a state transition under a fixed implementation. The outer transition concerns a change to the governing component or artifact version, not every change to its runtime inputs. Whether a learned procedure is treated as memory data or executable code must be declared before comparing adaptation mechanisms.

The state visible to the policy is usually not Markov. A summarized conversation may omit a pending asynchronous job, an already consumed credential, or a revoked approval. The full execution system can nevertheless maintain those facts in privileged state. Mixing privileged state into free-form prompts as the only enforcement mechanism sacrifices a useful separation: text is evidence to a stochastic policy, whereas authorization and commit status require explicit operational semantics. Chapter develops compatibility across these representations.

A simple counterexample shows why context length alone cannot measure continuity. Consider two histories with identical retained text: both say that a report should be uploaded. In one history the upload has already committed; in the other, the request timed out before any effect. A policy conditioned only on retained text cannot distinguish the states. Retrying is appropriate in one case and may duplicate an external effect in the other. Increasing the context window helps only if the distinguishing event is recorded, retained, interpretable, and consulted. A durable operation identifier and a reconciliation endpoint can resolve the ambiguity without increasing the model window.

For scientific comparison, the intervention unit should therefore be the configuration and its state initialization, not merely the model identifier. An experiment that compares two agents while silently changing the tool registry, memory contents, retry policy, or execution environment cannot attribute its outcome to one named mechanism. The configuration should include release or commit identities, and the trajectory should preserve enough information to reconstruct the actual observations that conditioned each action. Reconstruction is not assumed possible when tool outputs or eviction histories were never stored.

Operational definitions of AGI differ in breadth, level of performance, adaptation requirements, and autonomy. A useful survey must expose these commitments rather than define AGI as whatever a preferred benchmark measures. Chollet emphasizes skill acquisition and generalization relative to priors and experience; the Levels of AGI framework separates breadth and performance while discussing autonomy as an additional axis. These are measurement frameworks, not demonstrations that unrestricted general intelligence has been achieved .

Their foundational role must be separated from dated system examples. The inspected fifth revision of Levels of AGI retains classifications explicitly referring to September 2023; those examples are not an October 2026 assessment. Here AGI denotes a proposed operating claim over declared task families, adaptation access, resource constraints, human assistance, and failure tolerances. No finite family below is asserted to exhaust general intelligence.
For a task distribution , adaptation protocol , and resource envelope , let denote a task and the induced distribution of interaction trajectories. Define

The index ranges over declared families rather than an unspecified universe of possible tasks. The score is accompanied by failure severity, calibration, time, cost, and uncertainty. A system may improve in one coordinate and regress in another; a scalar average requires explicit weights and cannot erase those regressions. Autonomy is represented by the actions available under , the human intervention protocol, and the permitted horizon. A system evaluated with unrestricted expert rescue is not being tested under the same autonomy conditions as one operating without rescue.

Adaptation must also be bounded. Allowing a system to acquire new tools, query demonstrations, run arbitrary experiments, or repeatedly inspect evaluation feedback changes the task. These capabilities may be entirely legitimate, but they belong in and . A method that solves a task after extensive environment-specific search is evidence of competence under that search budget. It does not establish that the initial policy already possessed the procedure or that transfer will persist when feedback is unavailable.

The human reference population matters whenever comparisons use the word human. Domain experts, general workers, and untrained participants have different knowledge, tools, and time budgets. Comparisons should align access to external resources and account for the costs of human supervision or correction. Claims of parity across a selected set of tasks remain claims about that set. They cannot establish competence over unobserved physical, social, or scientific environments.

Generality and reliability interact. A broad system that occasionally performs well but fails unpredictably under repeated attempts may be less useful than a narrower system with a verified operating envelope. Evaluation should preserve task-level distributions and repeated-run outcomes. A frontier score is an observation about a measurement process; it becomes evidence of generality only after its distribution, leakage controls, resource conditions, and failure modes have been examined.

Let denote one coordinate of the competence profile with the model parameters and harness configuration exposed separately. Hold the task population, initialization, adaptation protocol, measurement apparatus, and complete resource envelope fixed. A two-model, two-harness comparison has interaction contrast

A nonzero contrast means that the harness difference depends on the evaluated model. An estimate requires paired tasks, repeated executions where stochasticity matters, and uncertainty that respects task clustering. It is a causal effect only under a valid intervention design; a cross-product of leaderboard entries with different budgets is insufficient.

The 27 October paper on the decision geometry of agent interfaces distinguishes a harness’s attainable regularized return from a deployed policy’s mismatch to it . Its exact identities assume finite states and actions, bounded rewards, discount below one, positive regularization, and positive reference support; stronger-model estimates in its coding study are proxies for the optimum. A fixed-policy harness comparison and a comparison after matched adaptation answer different questions. Harness Scaling likewise studies training over structured execution configurations and transfer to held-out harness combinations . Neither result makes arbitrary interface changes harmless. Adaptation cost, training-harness exposure, and held-out combinations must remain explicit when interpreting transfer as generality.

The corresponding HRP source separates those evidential levels. In environment/hrp_miniwob/oracle.py, solve and evaluate operate on a finite control graph; policy_metrics in environment/hrp_miniwob/measurements.py separately computes the return gap and occupancy-weighted divergence. The training route miniwob_v2_train.py uses an Exact-PG update through a verl worker, whereas StrongTeacherEstimator supplies deployment proxies . These paths were inspected without executing training. The repository’s environment documentation also maps code harness labels to paper labels; treating the two label orders as identical would misidentify the experimental intervention.

The distinction between component classes is functional. A tool is an invocation interface to an operation. A skill is procedural information, possibly including executable resources, that conditions how operations are chosen and composed. A protocol specifies exchanges and lifecycle semantics between participants. A session identifies and manages a sequence of interactions. A memory system determines how information is retained, revised, accessed, and forgotten. An SDK supplies construction interfaces; a managed platform operates selected mechanisms behind a service boundary. A product integrates them for a workload and user interface. One package may fulfill several roles with distinct contracts.

These distinctions prevent common category errors. A checkpoint can preserve a graph state without maintaining a correct semantic account of a user’s changing preferences. A vector store can retain records without teaching a policy when those records should influence action. A protocol-compliant server can return false information. A skill can be syntactically valid but obsolete after a tool-schema change. A large model can interpret all of these artifacts while still acting on stale authority. The mechanism required for each property must be tested at its own boundary.

The inspected October 2026 source revisions instantiate different persistence objects. OpenAI Agents Python defines conversational item persistence through Session; prepare_input_with_session separately prepares the model input and the new items eligible for persistence. LangGraph separates thread checkpoint/channel state from its cross-thread BaseStore. Google ADK separates a Session’s application, user, session identity, event history, and state from BaseMemoryService ingestion and search . These are inspected interfaces, not interchangeable semantic-memory guarantees. The retained object, the actual model request, and the authority to reuse an item require separate evidence.

Agent Lightning v1.0 makes the training boundary equally concrete: a deployment harness supplies interaction while captured model calls become training data . In the inspected source, ProxyRouter.prepare_body requests token identifiers and forward_request captures exchanges. In trajectory aggregation mode, RolloutAdapter.get_train_data_batch in agentlightning/verl/rollout_adapter.py merges compatible token prefixes and masks inserted observations. When enabled, compute_rollout_level_advantage groups captured samples by rollout identity and checks their shared task and reward . This supplies an implementation path for examining conditioning and credit assignment, not proof that every supported configuration reproduces the paper. The source was inspected rather than trained. A session trace becomes suitable policy-training evidence only after its action tokens, behavior inputs, probability semantics, and grouping survive the conversion.

The brain analogy is useful only at this functional level. Working context resembles a limited active information workspace; episodic records preserve aspects of past interaction; semantic records organize claims; procedural memory stores reusable action guidance. Model weights, KV tensors, event logs, and databases implement these functions through very different update and access rules. A KV cache is a set of computation-dependent tensors, not a faithful semantic archive. External record deletion does not erase parametric associations. The analogy provides a vocabulary for timescales and access, not evidence of neurological equivalence. Memory surveys organize this landscape through different axes, including agent versus model memory, active versus inactive representations, and resource–distortion tradeoffs; the component ontology here complements those taxonomies rather than claiming to replace them .

The literature and implementation review for all chapters extends through 29 October 2026; each source retains its reported revision and retrieval limits. Foundational methods are not excluded by age. Contemporary papers, official technical reports, normative specifications, and versioned repositories are examined according to the mechanism being claimed. First public release, manuscript revision, code release, and product activity are distinct dates. A 2026 revision of a 2025 paper is not automatically a newly introduced 2026 method. A university evaluation of a proprietary model is not research authored by that model’s vendor.

This is a mechanism-oriented critical survey, not a claim of exhaustive systematic identification. Candidate discovery combines a seed bibliography, citation following, and topic-specific searches for context editing, agent memory, procedural skills, tool protocols, harness optimization, agent evaluation, scientific agents, security, and serving. The present chapter additionally searches model–harness adaptation, pretraining capability elicitation, and harnessed reinforcement learning. Paper titles and identifiers are checked against original records; implementation claims use official repositories or documentation, with a commit, release, or protocol version when available. Retrieval occurred on 28–29 October 2026. The publication cutoff concerns artifact availability, not the calendar day on which an eligible artifact was inspected.

Inclusion requires a technical connection to an identified mechanism or evaluation boundary. Foundational references establish definitions, algorithms, or historical lineage; they do not substitute for current capability evidence. Frontier claims require an eligible primary artifact and retain its revision and experimental scope. A withdrawn manuscript does not support capability claims. Abstract-only or metadata-only inspection does not establish method details, and inaccessible implementation information remains an evidence gap. Organization-specific comparisons require verified paper affiliations rather than inferred ownership. Product catalogues provide ecosystem coverage, while feature and performance comparisons require additional mechanism-specific evidence.

For a mutable documentation page, the observation date and the available version have different meanings. A page read after the cutoff cannot establish that all of its present contents existed before the cutoff; a dated release or pinned artifact is needed for that historical claim. Consequently, the survey reports current mechanisms within the searched and inspected population rather than declaring any method universally best or all eligible work exhausted. Unresolved source leads are not counted as independently verified methods.

Four evidence classes are kept separate. An author-reported result is attributed to an exact source version and experimental setting. An independent reproduction requires actually executed artifacts, data identity, environment, configurations, seeds, and recorded outcomes. An analytical deduction follows from stated assumptions and may provide a bound, counterexample, or resource calculation. A proposed experiment defines a hypothesis and a discriminating intervention but has no observed result. This book does not present independent reproductions where none were performed.

Verification of a title and identifier does not verify a result. Inspection of a repository does not show that its current head reproduces a paper. A benchmark improvement does not prove the proposed mechanism caused the improvement unless resources and relevant alternatives are controlled. In particular, additional tool calls, longer reasoning, more candidates, or a stronger evaluator can account for gains attributed to a memory representation or orchestration strategy. The evidential question is the effect of the mechanism under declared operating conditions.

Conflicting findings are compared through task populations, resource accounting, feedback access, model versions, memory initialization, task order, and grading. Where these differences do not resolve the disagreement, the conflict remains open. A method can simultaneously improve average accuracy and worsen tail risk, or improve a selection score while losing held-out transfer. Those outcomes require a multi-dimensional interpretation rather than an editorial ranking. Evaluation frameworks such as HELM motivate systematic scenario and metric coverage, while agent benchmarks expose additional dependence on tool and environment semantics .

Agents’ Last Exam evaluates configured agents on an executed workflow population; an expanding advertised task collection is not that experiment’s denominator. Its mixed model–harness comparisons and fixed-harness backbone comparisons must remain distinct . AgentHorizon instead assesses judges on recorded instruction–trajectory pairs, including constructed near misses. It does not directly measure autonomous agent completion, and the constructed error distribution is not a natural deployment failure distribution . Table makes the different inference boundaries explicit. All empirical findings remain author-reported.

TraceTrial-Bench’s selected archive is not a set of independent repetitions within every model–harness–task cell. Its semantic scoring also resolves some unexercised harness criteria using task outcomes, so the two evaluation layers are not statistically independent. Automatically activated mechanism links are candidates, not validated causal propagation . ASAP’s reference-prefix interventions and Harness Scaling’s training exposure similarly belong in the experimental configuration . These limitations change what a score estimates; they are not repaired by adding another decimal place or averaging unlike benchmarks.

Identity is a relation among dated artifacts, rather than a string copied from a product list. A renamed project, acquired service, and rewritten SDK can share a commercial lineage while exposing different execution semantics. An alias record should therefore specify the entities, the relation, its effective interval, and the primary evidence. A merger does not prove API compatibility, and an organization named in an announcement does not establish every author’s affiliation. For an affiliation filter, the relevant observation is the author-to-institution statement in the inspected paper version; a repository owner or email domain is insufficient evidence of that paper’s institutional authorship. These distinctions prevent organizational metadata from becoming an unsupported proxy for technical quality.

Release dates also have different meanings. The first preprint, a revised method, a public repository commit, a package release, and hosted availability are separate events. A claim about the earliest available mechanism must identify which event is relevant and retain the version that contained it. A later revision cannot be assigned the earlier version’s date without checking that the mechanism was already present. Conversely, a preprint available before the literature cutoff remains eligible even when its stated conference occurs later. Dates establish availability, not independent validation or priority beyond the searched population.

Popularity measures need an equally explicit denominator. Repository stars, package downloads, public mentions, and service users measure different populations and have different duplication, access, and sampling effects. Record the platform, observation time, counting rule, entity identity, and missingness before comparing them. Such counts can describe visibility or adoption under that definition; they do not identify a capability ranking. A priority list can guide inspection without becoming evidence that its first entry is technically strongest.

An independent observatory supplies additional evidence only through a specified measurement protocol. Its task sample, evaluator, attempt budget, model endpoint, tool permissions, and observation date determine the estimand, just as they do for an author-run benchmark. Independence of organization does not guarantee independence of task data or judge errors. Agreement between two sites that reuse the same predictions is one result observed twice. Disagreement can instead arise from different configured systems or changing hosted versions. The appropriate synthesis preserves those boundaries and reports an unresolved comparison when they cannot be aligned.

The organizing synthesis separates three obligations that are often collapsed into a statement that an agent retained its state. Let denote a complete implementation state. Its projections include the model-visible context , tool interface , authoritative feasible-action set under current authority epoch , and an effect ledger . The ledger maps operation identifiers to typed states such as pending, reconciled success, reconciled failure, and unknown. These are semantic status classes, not unverified model assertions. The comparison holds external observations fixed. It requires preservation of operation identity and recorded status, including explicit uncertainty. It does not validate an initially incorrect ledger or undo external effects. Reconciliation that acquires new service evidence is a separate transition and can legitimately change an unknown status to confirmed success or failure. A pending or unknown outcome cannot become a proven failure merely because a summary omitted the operation.

The exact contracts , , and are logically independent. Consider a product state with separate context, permission, and ledger coordinates. Changing only a context bit that controls a deterministic proposal violates while preserving authority and the ledger. Changing only a permission coordinate from denied to allowed violates while leaving the proposal distribution and ledger unchanged. Changing only a recorded committed outcome to unknown violates while preserving context and permissions. Each construction is a witness that the other two predicates do not imply the third. The claim is not made for the vacuous tolerance . This is an analytical non-implication argument; it is not a claim of a new general theorem about cognition.

The distinction matters in actual mechanisms. Context editing and compaction primarily expose and behavior-conditioning obligations. Privilege monitors expose . Checkpoints and effect reconciliation expose . Memory updates and model migrations can affect all three. A verifier then tests a specified subset of the required properties; passing that verifier does not establish properties outside its scope. MemoryWalker addresses behavior-time conditioning and Progent privilege control . CyberGym-E2E’s vulnerability, proof-of-concept, and patch checks and AgentHorizon’s trajectory judgments test different outcome properties; neither demonstrates durable effect-ledger reconstruction .

The originality of this survey lies in analyzing those boundaries jointly, connecting their assumptions to identifiable implementations, and constructing interventions that distinguish their failures. It does not relabel context editing, rate-distortion analysis, privilege control, or durable execution as newly discovered ideas. Contemporary memory and compression surveys already organize substantial parts of that landscape . The added question is which contracts survive composition and co-adaptation, and what evidence can falsify that claim. Chapters , , , and develop the resulting conditioning, authority, recovery, and integration analyses.

A state transformation can preserve every proposal, permission, and ledger entry while preserving a wrong policy or an incorrect historical record. The three contracts therefore govern transformation integrity; task acceptance requires additional observed evidence. An operational implementation should return scoped verdicts and identify which evidence can resolve a failed or undecidable check. Merely adding a verifier whose output is always accepted would leave this distinction empty.

Let be finite and an evidence record binding source inputs, versions, current grants, and available receipts. With tolerance and authority epoch fixed, for let return failed, passed, or unresolved under a declared checking procedure. Define

Membership permits advancement under that procedure’s scope; admission expires when a governing state version or authority epoch changes. It establishes the mathematical contract only when the checker and its premises justify that inference. In particular, sampled behavioral agreement does not prove equality of proposal distributions. The diagnostic set selects a corrective evidence operation, rather than another undirected reflection.

Effect reconstruction and task validation also need separate outputs. For an operation identifier , let and be the corresponding effect-evidence and task-test projections of . Define as confirmed effect, confirmed absence, or unresolved status under the service contract, and as the verdict for a specified task property. Retain

Here absence concerns the specified effect, not a claim that no partial effect exists elsewhere. A confirmed upload can contain the wrong artifact; a valid local artifact can coexist with an unknown upload outcome. These observations demand different corrections. Current dispatch authorization remains necessary even after a transformation passes. New service evidence may legitimately revise ; it must be recorded as reconciliation, not disguised as preservation of the old ledger.

A discriminating study injects one conditioning, grant, or operation-record fault at a time into otherwise matched states. It reports false admission, unresolved decisions, recovery cost, and verified task outcomes separately. No outcome is presumed here: the construction specifies how the chapter’s three contracts become diagnosable engineering obligations.

The first question is whether retained information remains usable. A memory system can archive every event and still fail to retrieve a rare instruction before an irreversible action. Retrieval can succeed while the policy fails to recognize implicit relevance. A summary can preserve a fact while dropping its temporal qualifier. These are different failures, requiring separate measurements of retention, access, interpretation, influence, and execution. Treating all of them as recall produces misleading explanations.

The second question is whether the system acts under the history it is trained to assume. Context compaction changes conditioning. Training reconstructed trajectories that expose information unavailable during rollout can create leakage or support mismatch. MemoryWalker explicitly studies this problem, while Context Language Models make context editing part of the policy interface. Their relationship is a cross-layer issue: an editing policy, a learning objective, and a serving cache must agree about which history produced each action .

The third question concerns improvement. A system that accumulates successful procedures may become better on recurring tasks while growing less robust to novel environments. An evolving harness can overfit a finite selection set. An evaluator can drift as the executor changes. Recursive improvement requires distinguishing the quality of the executor from the quality of the process that proposes, selects, and validates future changes. RRSI and Harness2 provide concrete but bounded mechanisms to analyze; neither licenses a general claim of indefinite acceleration . The additional adaptation question is whether a revision improves its available control problem or merely fits the current policy; a frozen-policy ranking cannot settle that distinction. Section specifies the corresponding comparison boundary.

The fourth question is operational: which guarantees survive interruption, concurrency, migration, and partial failure? A correct answer in a clean benchmark environment may rely on assumptions absent in deployment. Duplicate actions, inconsistent checkpoints, stale indexes, revoked permissions, and unobserved external effects connect systems engineering directly to model behavior. Reliable autonomy is an end-to-end property of this coupled process. The subsequent chapters develop the mathematical, computational, and empirical machinery needed to test it.

Agent mathematics distinguishes the world, the system’s recorded information, and the inputs actually exposed to a decision rule. Let be latent environment state, an observation, and the filtration of recorded system observations and preceding actions before action . Let describe the information exposed to the proposal policy. Unlike the accumulated record, these exposed information sets need not be nested after compaction. A realizable stochastic policy is a -measurable probability kernel; sampling from it uses fresh randomization. Requiring the sampled action itself to be measurable before that randomization would exclude stochastic policies. Neither the kernel nor its input constructor may use tomorrow’s observations or hidden evaluation answers. This distinction identifies leakage without pretending that the agent observes the latent world.

OpenAI Agents Python’s prepare_input_with_session in src/agents/run_internal/session_persistence.py retrieves history under a configurable limit, merges history with new input, and returns prepared input separately from items eligible for persistence . A stored conversation cannot substitute for the conditioning input in a likelihood calculation. Instrumentation must retain the final model request after subsequent filters; comparing the store with this preparation stage alone would miss later edits.
Bayesian conditioning provides a useful abstraction for uncertain observations. Given a prior and observation likelihood ,

The displayed sum is for discrete or countable states and requires positive predictive probability for the observation. A zero denominator identifies no posterior under this model; it calls for a declared model-recovery or conservative fallback rule, not a zero vector or an arbitrary normalization. Continuous states require the corresponding integrals and regular conditional distributions. A retrieved statement should not automatically be treated as a noiseless observation of . Its reliability depends on source identity, timestamp, provenance, and the possibility of adversarial manipulation. Multiple retrieved passages may share a common origin and therefore fail to provide independent evidence. Multiplying their likelihoods as though they were independent can create extreme but unjustified confidence. The implementation analogue is to retain provenance links and deduplicate evidence lineages, rather than counting repeated text as corroboration.

Let denote interaction history and a compressed representation. Compression is useful when decisions can be made from with acceptable loss. Faithful text reconstruction is only one possible objective. A task may require preserving an authorization expiry time while allowing substantial paraphrase of everything else. Conversely, a summary with high lexical similarity may lose precisely the condition that changes the correct action.

The relevant target for control can be the optimal action, a value function, a constraint event, or a predictive distribution over consequences. These targets need not agree. A finite POMDP consists of latent states , actions , observations , transition probabilities , observation probabilities , a reward function, and an initial distribution. Zero-probability observations contribute nothing to a model expectation but cannot be silently normalized when actually encountered. Belief sufficiency assumes a correct closed Markov model; changing tool versions, budgets, or permissions require an augmented state . Tool environments rarely provide such a model explicitly. The belief-state formulation nevertheless clarifies what uncertainty remains after a tool response. An HTTP timeout can mean that a request never arrived, that it committed but its response was lost, or that it is still running. A belief over these states is more accurate than automatically labeling the action failed. A reconciliation query can have high value because it changes which retry decisions are safe.

Actions have different durations. A fixed per-action discount can favor one hour-long operation over several short checks even when their physical-time consequences differ. For a tiny discrete environment, exact belief filtering and dynamic programming can provide an oracle baseline. In a real repository, browser, or enterprise system the state space is combinatorial and the transition model changes. Approximate filters, structured event records, and conservative uncertainty handling become implementation choices. The formal model should guide which approximations are tested rather than imply that exact POMDP planning is tractable.

An agent often needs to estimate whether an answer is correct, whether retrieved evidence remains valid, or whether an operation will violate a constraint. For a predicted probability and binary outcome , calibration requires that events with predicted probability occur at frequency under the evaluated distribution. In conditional-expectation form, almost surely under that law . This score-level statement is weaker than identifying the full decision-information posterior . Calibration does not imply discrimination: a model that always predicts the base rate can be calibrated while failing to distinguish easy from hard cases. Ranking quality, probability calibration, and operational utility require separate evaluation.

Suppose executing an action yields known gain if correct and known loss if incorrect, while abstention has zero utility. If is the correctness probability conditional on the decision information, execution is preferable when

The threshold changes with consequence severity. Ordinary marginal calibration of a score is insufficient when errors or consequences vary with additional decision covariates; those covariates must be included or the utility evaluated within the appropriate strata. A confidence score calibrated on benign tool calls need not be calibrated on adversarially selected calls. Human escalation also has cost and delay, and may itself be fallible. Its value should be measured relative to a defined review process rather than treated as an infallible terminal action.
Chance constraints express a different objective. Let indicate whether a declared violation occurs within the finite horizon :

Estimating a small requires enough independent evidence about rare failures. Observing no violations in a small sample does not prove the probability is zero. Dependence across repeated sessions, shared memory, or common model failures reduces the information in nominal trial counts. A risk bound must identify both the sampling assumptions and the operational event being bounded.

Hard constraints can be enforced by a shield or validator that restricts the action set, but the guarantee is limited to the property that the validator actually checks. A schema validator can reject malformed arguments while accepting a well-formed unauthorized destination. A permission policy can restrict destinations while failing to detect false content. Composing controls requires examining whether their assumptions are compatible and whether one control changes the distribution seen by another.

Let be the outcome for task under method . A paired comparison uses differences so that task difficulty is controlled. If multiple trials share a user, repository, or persistent memory trajectory, those trials are not independent samples merely because they have different random seeds. The resampling unit should preserve the dependence structure. A bootstrap over individual messages can produce narrow intervals that ignore the variation between whole task sequences.

At the hypothetical value and , these are and . These are analytical illustrations under independence, not benchmark measurements. Real attempts can be correlated through shared prompts, retrieved memories, or common tool failures. Reported pass metrics must use the exact benchmark definition rather than inherit this toy model.

Adaptive method selection introduces another source of optimism. If many harnesses are evaluated on the same finite task set and the best is retained, the retained score is selected partly for favorable noise. A held-out set used repeatedly to decide which candidate to keep has become part of the selection process. The required separation is operational: an evaluator cannot remain an untouched test merely because its file is named test. RRSI regularizes harness proposals and selection, but its cost/novelty shaping can admit candidates within a noise band; this is not simultaneous certification of promotions .

Repeated looks at a fixed estimand and adaptive benchmark reuse are distinct. A confidence sequence supports optional stopping under its conditional stochastic assumptions ; it does not make candidates selected using the same task feedback independent of that feedback. REUSE instead proves simultaneous promotion control under an initially independent iid evaluation set, decision-only feedback, and error allocation over all possible promotion histories . With the round, the number of earlier promotions, tested candidates per history, and nonnegative weights predeclared before evaluation feedback and satisfying and , its allocation is

There are possible promotion histories and candidates at each, so the error budget summed over those tests is at most . Revealing arbitrary scores or traces violates the decision-only feedback premise. The reported experiment concerns classification-pipeline search on Covertype, not coding-agent or post-training validation. A theorem for that protocol is not a general guarantee for benchmark-guided self-improvement.

This follows by inverting . It is neither a proof that nor an authorization decision. If the checker can miss a true failure, the bound concerns detected failures unless its miss rate is independently bounded.

For the proposal contract, paired sampled actions are not automatically a test of total variation. Under a known complete alphabet of size , predeclared sample sizes and independent draws within each law, a simple subset-union bound gives, with probability at least ,

Indeed, apply Hoeffding to every subset of the outcomes, to both laws, and then use the triangle inequality. Large action alphabets make this bound weak. Authority and ledger equality can instead be checked exactly when their finite trusted sets and records are available; sampling their failures establishes only a distribution-scoped rate.

The mathematical object in a paper and the operational object in code must be connected by an explicit correspondence. State variables need storage locations and update semantics. Conditional probabilities need recorded conditioning inputs. An algorithm’s action set must match the tool registry and authority available during execution. A complexity expression needs tensor shapes, precision, batch structure, and communication assumptions. A confidence interval needs a sampling unit and a treatment of missing outcomes. These are not documentation details added after the science; they determine which claim the implementation actually tests.

A useful validation procedure begins with a minimal environment whose latent state is fully known. Introduce one controlled departure at a time: omitted observations, delayed tool responses, a lossy context transform, a stale memory, an evolving schema, or a noisy verifier. Check that the observed failure matches the mechanism predicted by the formal model. This establishes a diagnostic connection before attempting large-scale benchmark comparisons. It does not substitute for realistic evaluation, because the minimal environment may omit the interactions that dominate deployment.

The most useful deductions are often impossibility or insufficiency results. If two histories are aliased by a representation but their required-action sets are disjoint, no downstream deterministic decoder with only that representation can satisfy both requirements. Figure gives the unique-optimum case. If a behavior policy assigns zero probability to an action needed by the target policy, importance sampling cannot estimate that target outcome from the observed support. If two systems receive different evaluator information, an accuracy difference does not isolate the proposed learning mechanism. These observations limit overclaiming and identify the additional instrumentation or intervention required to make progress.

A proposed diagnostic reports checker errors, observable contract failures, unresolved verdicts, task outcomes, and recovery cost separately. It freezes the candidate during the stated validation regime or explicitly changes the estimand when policy or persistent state adapts. An unknown service outcome must not disappear merely because it is difficult to score.

The remaining chapters apply these principles to model interfaces, latent representations, context transformations, memory transactions, tool protocols, evaluation, and infrastructure. Mathematical precision is valuable when it changes the experiment or implementation decision. A symbolic objective without a realizable information set or a measurable failure event provides little assurance about an autonomous system.

These mechanisms differ from merely allocating an ordinary dense cache more efficiently. Their correctness and quality depend on a model trained with those structural choices, so they cannot be applied as a transparent replacement for every earlier checkpoint.

Bind each reuse invariant, approximation, and quality test to the checkpoint and implementation. A model-specific compression method can preserve aggregate long-context scores while failing these rare distinctions. Conversely, a specialized architecture may achieve substantial resource savings without sacrificing the tested distinctions. The result must remain attached to the actual mechanism and workload rather than a generic claim of superior memory.

An agent system constructs the input, interprets sampled outputs, and controls their external effects. The proposal and execution distributions are normalized only when invalid, denied, and terminated-without-operation outcomes remain represented. This distribution is not obtained by renormalizing over feasible actions unless the executor actually resamples until acceptance under the corresponding assumptions. Proposal quality, refusal behavior, and executed-action quality therefore require separate denominators. This distinction connects the model boundary to the authority contract in Chapter .

The context constructor, decoding rule, and interpreter are therefore part of the deployed policy. Temperature changes the distribution before interpretation. A grammar mask removes sequences. A retry loop conditions the eventual output on previous failures. A tool router can remap a nominal operation to a different implementation. Comparing two checkpoints while changing these mechanisms does not isolate a model effect. Conversely, a harness can improve end-to-end reliability without changing any model parameter. The agent-computer interface studied in SWE-agent is a concrete demonstration that the interface deserves independent analysis, although its reported task results do not imply a universal interface advantage .

The state exposed to the model need not be the complete execution state. A scheduler may retain locks, transactions, budgets, or authorization decisions outside . Denote complete system state by , where is environment state and collects compatible versions. The implemented transition has the form . A language model only parameterizes one conditional component. Statements that the model remembers, plans, or recovers should specify which information and transitions are supplied by the surrounding system. Otherwise a property of durable storage can be incorrectly attributed to model weights.

An important consequence concerns evaluation units. A successful sampled completion is evidence about the composition of model and decoder under one context. A successful completed task is evidence about a trajectory through a particular harness and environment. A successful resumed task additionally tests state reconstruction. These events have different denominators. A model that emits more valid JSON may still perform fewer useful operations if the schema encourages an incorrect decomposition. A smaller model can outperform a larger one when its tool arguments are calibrated to the available interface. Neither observation establishes a general ranking without matched tasks and resources.

For implementation, the policy boundary should expose the exact serialized request, model and tokenizer identities, decoding settings, selected tool schema, raw output, parsed output, and execution outcome. Sensitive fields can be redacted in an audit representation, but their existence and transformations must remain identifiable. Logging only the final natural-language answer destroys evidence needed to distinguish a model error from parser repair or tool failure. This is particularly damaging during post-training: the gradient must be associated with the conditions under which an action was actually generated, rather than a convenient reconstruction assembled after the task.

Let be a byte string and a canonical encoding into token indices . Its teacher-forced token likelihood factors as , with termination handled under a declared convention. A per-token loss depends on and cannot directly rank byte-level predictive efficiency across tokenizers. For a fixed corpus of byte strings, a useful operational quantity is total negative log probability in base two divided by the total number of original bytes. Report normalization and boundary-token conventions with that code-length measure.

Canonical-encoding likelihood is also distinct from the probability of a decoded byte string when several token sequences decode to it: the latter sums their sequence probabilities. A lossy normalizer can additionally map distinct original byte strings to the same encoding. These distinctions matter when assigning probabilities to exact tool arguments. BPE merges frequent adjacent units; SentencePiece supplies tokenization with explicit normalization choices. Neither mechanism alone establishes the optimal vocabulary for every language, codebase, or tool protocol .

An agent handles material with very different token statistics: prose, source code, URLs, paths, JSON, tables, OCR output, and arbitrary identifiers. A tokenizer that is economical on conversational English can fragment a long hexadecimal identifier into many pieces. That fragmentation increases context consumption and the number of predictions needed to reproduce an argument exactly. It can also alter where truncation occurs. A context limit expressed as a token count is consequently a capacity of a specific encoder, not a language-independent quantity of evidence. Cross-model memory comparisons should report the underlying content and its encoded length for each tokenizer.

Normalization introduces a second issue. Unicode composition, whitespace treatment, casing, and byte fallback influence whether encoding and decoding preserve a tool argument exactly. Human-readable equivalence does not imply operational equivalence. A database key can distinguish two strings that render similarly; a shell interpreter can assign meaning to whitespace that a prose normalizer treats as redundant. The relevant invariant for an execution boundary is for the supported domain, with the domain explicitly stated. If preprocessing intentionally changes , the system should retain the original bytes and the transformation rather than describing the result as lossless tokenization.

A tokenizer is not an authorization mechanism. Reserved role markers and tool delimiters can assist serialization, but the application must control which message fields can introduce them. An untrusted document containing the spelling of a privileged marker must remain document content. The parser and transport determine authority; the statistical model can still be influenced by a convincing imitation even when the actual privilege boundary is preserved. This distinction is central to prompt injection. Preventing a byte sequence from becoming a system message is necessary, while preventing every semantic influence from untrusted content is a separate learning and control problem.

Vocabulary size creates an engineering tradeoff. With hidden width and vocabulary size , an untied output projection has parameters and computes a distribution over alternatives at each prediction. Tying input and output embeddings reduces stored parameters but does not remove the output computation. Increasing can shorten sequences while increasing projection cost and making rare units harder to estimate. The optimum depends on corpus composition, architecture, batch shape, and hardware. It cannot be selected solely by minimizing tokens per character. A multilingual agent should also examine whether equal task budgets allocate systematically different usable text across languages.

The Transformer makes a position-dependent representation by mixing previous token representations through attention and applying learned nonlinear transformations. For one attention head, , , and , with defining the output under additive mask . A causal mask prevents access to future positions. This is a constraint on the computational graph, not a claim that the representation is a faithful account of everything in the past. Positional information, finite precision, training distribution, and learned attention patterns all affect what historical evidence influences a decision .

Dense attention offers direct content-dependent access to retained positions, with quadratic attention arithmetic during a full sequence pass. A recurrent architecture compresses past information into a bounded state. Transformer-XL introduces segment-level recurrence, while selective state-space models such as Mamba use input-dependent state updates designed for efficient sequence processing . The important comparison for agents is not whether an architecture has memory in an informal sense. It is what can be retained, accessed, modified, or invalidated under a fixed storage and computation envelope. A recurrent state can be compact while losing a rare constraint that an external event log still preserves.

Consider a deterministic recurrent update . If two distinct histories map to the same , every subsequent decision based only on that state must treat them identically until new observations distinguish them. When the histories require different authorized actions, this state aliasing imposes an irreducible error for that interface. Attention can avoid that particular collision by retaining explicit positions, but it does not eliminate errors of selection or interpretation. External retrieval changes the accessible evidence again. Consequently, a fair comparison must hold the external memory service constant or explicitly attribute gains to the combined architecture.

Rotary position embeddings encode relative phase relationships in queries and keys. Their algebraic ability to evaluate larger positions does not establish useful reasoning at those positions . Extending a context window can change frequency regimes, attention distributions, and numerical behavior. An agent with a long session also encounters a nonuniform evidence distribution: recent tool responses, early user constraints, and intermediate summaries have different roles. Tests that merely insert one recoverable string into a long input do not fully measure the ability to reconcile those roles. Nominal length and effective decision context therefore require separate reporting.

Mixture-of-experts architectures introduce conditional parameter activation. A router selects a small subset of experts for each token, so total stored parameters exceed the parameters active in one forward path . This can improve the capacity-to-compute tradeoff, but expert weights still occupy memory and communication can dominate when routing crosses devices. An agent workload with small batches and heterogeneous contexts may exercise a different routing and communication regime from the large packed sequences used in training. Total parameter count is thus insufficient to predict latency, cost, or quality. Active FLOPs, resident memory, expert imbalance, and interconnect behavior belong in the comparison.

Grouped-query attention shares key and value heads across groups of query heads. It reduces the dimensionality of cached keys and values while retaining multiple query projections . The reduction in KV storage is exact for a specified layout; the quality effect is empirical and depends on training or conversion. Calling grouped-query attention a larger context mechanism is incomplete: it makes a given capacity cheaper, but does not guarantee that the model uses additional historical information correctly. The distinction matters when a product increases the advertised window after an infrastructure change without changing its evidence-use evaluation.

Multi-head latent attention uses a different factorization. The DeepSeek-V3 report’s Section 2.1.1 jointly compresses content keys and values into a latent vector and retains a separate rotary-position component . In schematic column-vector notation, let , , and . The content score obeys , allowing a compatible implementation to score against the compressed state without storing every expanded content key. The separate positional contribution must still be handled; ignoring it does not reproduce the trained attention computation.

If the retained latent has dimension and the extra positional key has dimension , an ideal per-token cache stores elements instead of for ordinary equal-width multi-head keys and values. This is a shape-based accounting identity, not a quality guarantee or an assertion that every implementation achieves the ideal storage. Up-projection arithmetic, query transformations, tensor layout, and kernel support affect performance. For an agent, this architecture changes the cost of preserving a long interaction history while leaving the separate question of decision-relevant recall unresolved. It should be compared with grouped-query and sparse-attention alternatives under matched quality and actual serving workloads.

Its Section 3 specifies joint attention to shared and local entries in one softmax . This is architectural recurrence within token prediction. It is neither a store of user sessions nor an ordinary deeper network with independently parameterized layers. The same parameters participate repeatedly, changing the computation and gradient paths without multiplying the stored block weights.

Their ratio is . At , , and , it is 0.2125. This calculated storage ratio does not imply a comparable reduction in computation: every recursion still evaluates the shared stack, and later queries read both shared and local evidence. Under the same simplified per-token read model, the extra local attention entries are a fraction of the separate-cache baseline.

Parameter sharing also constrains the function class. Repeating one transformation does not reproduce an arbitrary sequence of independently trained transformations, while explicit shared-cache access changes the available state at each recursion. A useful experiment separates weight tying, recursion count, local-window size, and shared-cache visibility at matched training exposure. Detaching the shared-cache gradient path tests a different mechanism from merely preventing later recursions from reading it. The source study analyzes these distinctions, but no universal benefit of increasing recursion depth follows from the architecture alone.

For agents, internal recursion spends computation without acquiring a new external observation. It can refine a prediction from existing evidence, but cannot resolve an unobserved transaction outcome by itself. Its cache remains tied to the model computation and does not establish durable cross-session memory. Compare extra internal recursions with external sampling, tool verification, or another observation under a declared cost envelope. These alternatives supply different information, so both their resource use and their evidence access must be reported when attributing gains to deeper reasoning.

A hypothetical calculation makes tokenizer interaction explicit. Suppose two tokenizers encode the same complete interaction in 100,000 and 125,000 tokens. The total compute ratio lies between these values when both components have positive cost and all other terms are unchanged. This is a deduction about a simplified accounting model, not a measured speedup or a realistic claim that two different models differ only in tokenization. Actual kernels, padding, caching, and data movement can change wall-clock behavior substantially.

At the action level, the expected cost also includes failed serializations. If one independent attempt costs and has probability of passing a syntactic validator, unbounded retries have expected attempt count when . This calculation says nothing about semantic correctness. A parser can accept a dangerous or irrelevant action. With at most attempts, the success probability under the same independence assumption is , and the expected number of attempts is . Correlated errors, state changes between attempts, or adaptive repair invalidate the simple model and must be measured rather than assumed away.

An agent comparison should therefore report valid-action rate, task success, input and output bytes, model-specific token counts, actual calls, tool expenditure, and wall-clock distribution. A price per million output tokens is not a task cost when one system repeatedly replays a long history or performs more retries. A faster kernel can free a budget that the harness then spends on additional search. Whether that improves reliability is an empirical question. Resource savings should be measured at both the model-call boundary and the complete task boundary to avoid converting an implementation improvement into an unsupported capability claim.

A typed action interface should distinguish prediction, validation, authorization, execution, and observation. Prediction selects a candidate operation and arguments. Validation checks syntax and local invariants. Authorization checks whether the candidate is permitted in the current state. Execution applies the operation. Observation reports what actually happened, including partial completion. Combining these stages into a single model-generated sentence removes useful control points. It also makes failures difficult to attribute: a statement that a file was updated may describe intent rather than an observed state transition.

Let indicate structural validity and indicate current authorization. A gated execution wrapper applies an operation only when both predicates hold. It should not assume that authorization inferred when constructing remains valid when the operation executes. Permissions can be revoked, resources can change, and another agent can acquire a lock. The model’s description of permission is evidence about its belief, not the permission itself. The authoritative check belongs to the execution boundary. This remains true even if the model was trained extensively on compliant demonstrations.

Schema-constrained decoding removes token sequences that cannot be extended into valid outputs. This can improve syntactic validity but changes the sampling distribution. If the unmasked probabilities are and the allowed set is , the constrained distribution is for , assuming ordinary renormalization and positive allowed mass. If , this formula is undefined; the implementation must return an explicit generation failure or a separately specified fallback, not divide by zero. Likewise an empty feasible grammar continuation and a length-truncated valid prefix need distinct outcomes. A likelihood computed without the same mask is not the likelihood of the deployed action generator. The distinction becomes consequential in policy optimization, calibration, and off-policy analysis. Grammar versions and tool schemas should therefore be versioned alongside the checkpoint and tokenizer.

An abstract execution boundary can be specified as a composition with explicit rejection branches. Let be the selected tool schemas, their configuration record, and the serialization map. With decoder and deterministic interpreter as defined in Section ,

The validity predicate assigns zero to the invalid symbol and to schema violations. It checks the selected interface rather than silently repairing its meaning. Only when does the runtime obtain a current authoritative read , refresh its execution state as , and evaluate . The read supplies current service state and the applicable authority epoch. Let and be distinct non-execution outcomes for invalidity and denial. Let identify the logical operation instance and its immutable arguments, with retries of that instance retaining the same identity. Let execute an operation under identity , with external randomness , and let record the returned evidence and configuration. The boundary returns

Execution appears only in the authorized branch. State refresh and authorization must be synchronized with dispatch under the service contract; writing this composition does not prove distributed atomicity. The observation record can contain failure, partial completion, or an unknown outcome; it does not turn a returned message into proof of a durable effect. These maps specify implementation obligations, not properties automatically supplied by an SDK. Duplicate-effect prevention additionally requires service-appropriate idempotency semantics for ; a random request identifier alone is insufficient.

Tool descriptions are themselves inputs to the model. Their ordering, length, examples, and similarity can influence routing, even when every description is accurate. A model can also infer unavailable capabilities from familiar tool names. Robust interfaces return explicit unsupported-operation failures and avoid describing aspirational features as installed functionality. Toolformer studies learning to insert API calls under specific data and filtering conditions; its method is relevant to learning this interface, but it does not establish correctness for arbitrary tool inventories or changing enterprise permissions .

An implementation record should separate architecture configuration from model weights, tokenizer artifacts, and policy-wrapper code. The configuration specifies head counts, sharing patterns, dimensions, positional treatment, context limits, and expert routing where applicable. The tokenizer record specifies vocabulary, merge rules or learned model, normalization, special tokens, and decoder behavior. The wrapper record specifies message serialization, grammar masks, parser handling, retries, and routing. A single model name rarely fixes all three. Reproduction requires immutable artifacts or hashes and a statement of any unavailable component.

The appropriate experiment is a factorial comparison rather than a universal leaderboard. Hold a checkpoint fixed while varying tokenizer-compatible serialization, schema ordering, constrained versus unconstrained decoding, and parser behavior. Separately compare model checkpoints under a common wrapper when their interfaces permit it. Include exact-copy tasks for identifiers, multilingual instructions, code editing, and multi-step tools with changing state. The outcome set should include useful task completion, rejected operations, invalid arguments, permission violations, and resource consumption. These measurements identify whether a change improves language modeling, interface compatibility, or the execution policy.

For architecture comparisons, define the resource axis before selecting models. Matching total parameters favors some sparse architectures; matching active FLOPs ignores resident memory; matching wall-clock time depends on implementation maturity. Report several axes when feasible and avoid declaring a single comparison intrinsically fair. A recurrent model with external retrieval should be compared with attention models using the same retrieval service, plus an ablation without retrieval. Otherwise memory infrastructure can conceal the architecture’s actual failure mode. Token budgets should be translated into underlying bytes and evidence units as well as reported in native tokens.

Contamination controls extend to tools and interfaces. A benchmark can leak its expected API names or canonical action traces even if final answers are held out. Split by task template, environment instance, and repository lineage where those structures matter. Randomize harmless tool ordering to test sensitivity while retaining a fixed canonical order for the main result. Use paired task instances and repeated runs to distinguish stable gains from sampling variation. A changed model response format should not silently invalidate the baseline parser; both systems need a documented, equally capable integration.

The expected failure taxonomy is mechanistic. Segmentation failures corrupt exact strings; serialization failures cross message boundaries; contextual failures omit relevant constraints; routing failures select a wrong operation; authorization failures execute an impermissible one; semantic failures produce a valid but ineffective action. These categories can co-occur and should not be forced into a single label when evidence is ambiguous. A retained raw request and observed transition allow later reclassification. Without that evidence, a reported model mistake may actually be an execution race or a lossy context transformation.

The foundation model is a conditional computation embedded in a stateful control system. Its capabilities remain important: stronger representations, broader training coverage, and better action distributions can reduce the burden on the harness. Nevertheless, the useful unit of analysis is the composition of tokenization, conditioning, decoding, interpretation, and execution. A model can only act on information available through that composition. Persistent storage helps only when the evidence reaches a representation and interface through which it can affect the correct decision.

This observation constrains claims about memory and self-improvement. Replacing a tokenizer or changing special-message serialization can alter the meaning of a stored token sequence even if the original text survives. Updating model weights can change how a procedural memory is interpreted. A context-editing harness can invalidate cached computational state. Compatibility is therefore more than a database schema version: it includes the model, tokenizer, prompt construction, action grammar, tool semantics, and authorization epoch. The detailed consistency analysis in Chapter builds on these interfaces rather than treating memory as an isolated retrieval component.

The engineering implication is to maintain explicit boundaries while studying their interactions. Save canonical external records in a representation that preserves their intended semantics and provenance, reconstruct model-specific inputs under a declared policy, and evaluate behavior after every material interface change. Do not infer indefinite competence from a larger window, universal memory from a recurrent state, or safe execution from valid JSON. Each property has a measurable operational definition, a specific implementation boundary, and failure conditions that can be tested independently before assessing the complete agent.

The state-aliasing argument can be strengthened into a decision bound. Suppose two histories occur with probabilities and , produce the same exposed state , and require distinct unique correct actions . Assume no additional observation arrives before the action. Any randomized policy conditioned only on has success probability

The proof uses : the linear objective is maximized by allocating all probability to the more frequent required action. Hence the minimum error is at least . This is an elementary deduction under the stated observational restriction, not a new impossibility result for any particular architecture. External retrieval can remove the restriction by supplying evidence that distinguishes the histories. A permission check can prevent execution of a wrong action, but cannot reconstruct the missing task information by itself.

This bound suggests a targeted architectural evaluation. Construct paired histories that differ in one decision-critical fact, then measure whether the system’s retained representation and available retrieval preserve that distinction. Keep the final query identical. Include an explicit-record baseline, a recurrent-state-only baseline where accessible, and an external-memory baseline with equal retrieval budgets. Balance the two histories so that a default action cannot obtain a misleadingly high score through prior frequency. The test measures a particular lost distinction; it cannot establish that every important distinction survives. Nevertheless, it is more diagnostic than averaging many easy tasks whose correct action is unchanged by the omitted history.

FlashAttention-4 addresses Blackwell through a redesigned asynchronous pipeline, tensor-memory use, software-assisted exponentials, and a two-CTA backward strategy. Its Section 5 reports B200 BF16 results up to 1613 TFLOPs/s, with maxima of against cuDNN 9.13 and against its Triton comparator. The paper’s Figure 4 also states that newer cuDNN versions incorporated related techniques and reached similar performance . Those version-qualified observations rule out using the original maximum as a timeless vendor-library ranking.

The pinned forward class is FlashAttention ForwardSm100 in flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm100.py, with mma_ping_pong_qk, softmax_loop, and correction_loop; FlashAttention BackwardSm100 is in the corresponding backward module . The important comparison with FA3 is the placement and overlap of work on hardware resources, not a different semantic attention objective. A faster matrix engine can leave exponentials or shared-memory traffic dominant. A correction stage removed from a critical path can help even when total arithmetic remains similar. This is why counting FLOPs alone can miss the mechanism of a kernel improvement.

An independent resource model makes the implication explicit. Let a tile require matrix time , nonlinear time , and movement time on separately overlappable resources. An ideal pipeline cannot complete faster than per steady-state tile. Doubling only matrix throughput replaces by ; when already exceeds , the full twofold gain is impossible without changing nonlinear work or overlap. This deduction does not require assigning an invented bandwidth to B200. It explains which measured counters could falsify a proposed bottleneck account.

Software approximations of elementary functions additionally need numerical auditing. The relevant comparison includes error before and after conversion to the attention input precision, extremes of the logit distribution, and repeated long-sequence reductions. Approximation of an exponential within an implementation is different from removing attention positions. Both can alter output, but their error models differ. A code review should trace the selected architecture, dtype, head dimensions, and compile-time options to the actual path rather than assuming that installation of a library guarantees a particular kernel executes.

For agent serving, benchmark the selected FA4 path under both large prefills and the service’s actual decode shapes, then inspect end-to-end task latency. Preserve a versioned cuDNN or alternative comparator, because a later library update can absorb the same optimization. Separate compilation time from execution time when evaluating a DSL-based implementation: faster iteration can be valuable even when steady-state kernel throughput is matched. None of these measurements establish better long-context reasoning without a quality test. The kernel contribution is reduced cost of a specified computation; the agent contribution is what useful decisions that computation enables under the released resource budget.
