Here are channel-group count, slots per group and slot width (with for a single group), and is the stored bits per scalar. Under a fixed task distribution and nonnegative predictive-distribution loss (such as log loss), one possible joint design objective is

The weights convert transmitted bits and end-to-end time to the chosen objective units. This is a comparison formulation, not the objective attributed to either paper. Frozen-backbone methods restrict the trainable parameters to adapters, compressors, or readers. A reconstruction objective and a task objective impose different information preferences; successful reconstruction is not sufficient for correct action, while task-only optimization can discard distinctions needed by future requests outside the training distribution.

The channel’s nominal payload is bits before headers and error-control overhead, but token count is an inadequate measure of its cost. The sender may process every evidence token, the receiver attends to slots at selected layers, and each sequential agent can retain a growing cache. Count transmitted tensors, storage copies, dtype conversions, encoder FLOPs, additional receiver attention, and device transfers. A comparison that charges generated text tokens to a text team while excluding latent tensors and extra hidden-state computation gives the methods different accounting boundaries. Conversely, text may be repeatedly tokenized and prefetched when a packet is reusable; reuse count and cache policy must therefore be matched.

Compatibility is semantic as well as dimensional. A width-matching projection does not establish that a new receiver assigns the same meaning to an old packet. Replacing the sender checkpoint, changing selected layers, quantizing the packet, or retraining the decoder changes the channel. Record an encoder–packet–reader compatibility identity and test migration with frozen packets as well as regenerated packets. If only regenerated packets work, the system has demonstrated a new channel, not backward-compatible memory. A context packet also needs source identity, validity interval, permissions, and deletion dependencies outside its latent values; a dense vector cannot be assumed to carry an enforceable authority label.

The inspected LatComm implementation makes this boundary identifiable: LatentBridge.compress constructs the packet, LatCommModel.encode_context obtains its encoder input, LatentInjector inserts receiver-side transformations, and PacketCache manages stored packets . These callable definitions were read at a dated source revision; they were not executed here. Their existence establishes an implementation path, not numerical parity with the paper or robust compatibility after modification.

The packet shape and cache key matter in the released code. LatentBridge.compress returns one slot array per paired layer, so a context packet is , not merely . PacketCache selects that packet by a hash of context text and loads its stored dtype; this lookup does not itself validate an encoder–reader compatibility identity. The generation path computes prompt-conditioned gates and reuses them during decoding . These observations bound the implementation claim: a wrapper must bind cache namespace and packet generation to the selected checkpoints and layer pairs. A matching text hash, shape or dtype alone does not establish semantic compatibility, and storage at 16 bits does not imply every consumer-side copy remains 16-bit. No mismatched-cache benchmark outcome is asserted.

A discriminating experiment compares raw text, equal-byte text compression, a single-vector representation, and a multi-slot channel under the same sender evidence, receiver, task stream, and total compute envelope. Include unseen questions about a fixed document and new document types; a query-independent packet should be tested on questions unavailable when it was encoded. Swap in mismatched packets as a negative control, remove the channel, and vary packet precision. Measure action correctness, contradiction handling, calibration, and effect-policy compliance alongside bandwidth and latency distributions. For model migration, cross old and new encoder–reader pairs and retain the off-diagonal failures. A large speed gain on repeated multiple-choice reading would remain useful, but would not by itself establish reliable sharing of open-ended plans, revocable authority, or concurrent agent state.

Shared memory is a distributed database whose contents influence policy. Consequently, concurrency errors can become reasoning errors. Two agents may update a fact from different observations, overwrite each other’s progress, or retrieve an obsolete skill after another worker changes its assumptions. The required consistency level depends on the record’s semantics. Append-only evidence can often tolerate concurrent insertion; a current authorization grant cannot be resolved by choosing whichever natural-language summary sounds more persuasive.

Separate immutable observations from mutable interpretations. Observations carry source, time, object version, and principal. Interpretations cite the observations they depend on and declare a validity interval. A correction can then invalidate an interpretation without destroying the evidence explaining why it was previously adopted. This structure supports both auditing and policy migration. It also prevents a deduplication routine from merging contradictory evidence into a falsely certain consensus.

Optimistic concurrency control is useful when updates are infrequent relative to reads. A worker reads version , computes a candidate update, and commits only if the stored version remains . On conflict it must re-evaluate the update against current state. Automatically replaying the old text can reintroduce a revoked fact. The conflict handler is therefore part of the policy interface, not simply a database retry loop.

Different merge functions have different algebraic properties. Set union is associative and commutative for immutable evidence identifiers. Last-writer-wins is operationally simple but uses clock order as a surrogate for semantic authority. Confidence-weighted merging can be misleading when confidence estimates share a common source or when the older record is more authoritative. A memory service should expose the selected rule and its assumptions rather than claim that all conflicts are solved by embeddings.

Procedural memory adds compatibility constraints. HyperSkill organizes skills and subtasks through trajectory hyperedges and maintenance operations . This offers a concrete mechanism for relational reuse, but a shared deployment must additionally define whether two workers may prune or merge the same skill concurrently. The paper’s sequential evaluation does not establish those concurrency semantics. A production adaptation should isolate maintenance, version skill identities, and preserve references from trajectories whose interpretation would otherwise change.

Evaluation should inject conflicting writes with known authority order, not merely test that both records appear in storage. Measure lost updates, stale reads that change decisions, unauthorized cross-user retrieval, and reproducibility of replay. Include a simple isolated-memory baseline: sharing is beneficial only when the transferred information improves the receiving task enough to justify contention, contamination, and governance complexity.

Every delegated operation needs an owner responsible for its budget, authority, cancellation, and final integration. A manager that starts workers and then terminates can leave active processes with no accountable controller. Ownership should be represented in execution state, with child operations linked to parent task and policy epochs. A child cannot acquire permissions merely because its parent was authorized to delegate reasoning.

Delegation authority is narrower than tool authority. A worker may be allowed to inspect a repository but not publish a branch, or to retrieve enterprise documents but not export them. Passing an unrestricted service credential to every worker defeats role isolation. Capability-scoped credentials and application-enforced tool registries make the distinction executable. The language model’s stated role is useful task guidance, but it is not an access-control boundary.

Cancellation has two meanings: stop producing additional work and stop all ongoing effects. The former may be achievable immediately; the latter can require tool-specific termination or reconciliation. If one worker completes the task, cancelling redundant workers should not discard evidence of requests already dispatched. The system needs an outstanding-operation set and a rule for handling late responses. Otherwise a result can arrive after the manager has finalized and silently mutate shared memory.

Failure propagation should distinguish dependent and independent branches. If a shared prerequisite is invalidated, every descendant that used it may require reevaluation. An unrelated worker can continue. This can be implemented with artifact dependency digests rather than broad restart signals. A global restart is simpler but increases cost and can repeat external effects. Overly narrow invalidation is cheaper but risks integrating work derived from obsolete premises.

The tail behavior of a team often depends on stragglers. Waiting for every worker maximizes coverage but can make latency dominated by one failed dependency. Quorum completion can reduce latency but changes the evidence population and may systematically omit difficult or dissenting analyses. The stopping rule should specify whether missing workers count as failures, censored observations, or intentionally unused candidates. A post hoc choice of whichever stopping rule makes the run look best is evaluation leakage.

Fault-injection tests should combine worker loss, delayed messages, policy revocation, and shared-store outages. Independent single faults are easier to diagnose, but correlated failures are operationally important: one tool outage can affect all workers, while one poisoned shared memory can redirect the whole team. Report containment and benign completion together. A coordinator that avoids every incident by refusing delegation has not demonstrated useful orchestration.

A factorial design can vary decomposition, communication, model diversity, and memory sharing. The basic conditions are a single agent, serial specialists, parallel independent specialists, and communicating specialists. Each uses the same task set, tool fixtures, evaluator access, and resource accounting. The design should declare whether it matches money, tokens, elapsed time, or more than one envelope. Different matches answer different questions; they should not be mixed into one headline ranking.

For a fixed task instance , define the paired gain . Average gains should be accompanied by their distribution over task families and difficulty strata. A positive mean can hide large regressions in tasks requiring coherent global context. Repeated model samples are nested within task instances, and shared persistent memory can induce dependence across tasks. Resampling individual calls as if they were independent produces overly narrow uncertainty intervals.

Communication ablations should preserve available information when possible. Removing all messages can change both coordination and evidence access. A stronger control supplies the same evidence through a deterministic aggregator while removing agent discussion. Conversely, randomizing or delaying selected messages tests whether timing and ordering drive the result. Such interventions can distinguish helpful information exchange from social anchoring or redundant narration.

Verifier access must be matched. A team with a dedicated critic effectively has more inference and perhaps additional tools. Compare it with a single agent receiving the same executable feedback, and with independent candidates selected by the same critic. If the gain comes from the critic rather than collaboration, the result still matters, but the mechanism should be named accurately. A critic’s agreement is not oracle truth; its false acceptance and false rejection require independent audit.

The main failure taxonomy separates decomposition errors, worker errors, communication loss, shared-state conflict, integration errors, and verifier errors. A final wrong answer may involve several stages. Assigning all failures to the last agent obscures causal structure. Use seeded faults and counterfactual replay to test whether replacing a particular message or artifact changes the outcome. Replay is informative only when external state and model nondeterminism are controlled or explicitly accounted for.

These experiments are a proposed research program rather than results established by the cited frameworks. Their practical value is to make a claim such as multi-agent reasoning helps operational. The claim becomes a statement about a particular topology, information protocol, task distribution, and budget. That precision allows disagreement between studies to be investigated rather than averaged away.

The October 2026 coding-team study directly varies which workflow stage receives workers: planning, implementation or verification . In its ProgramBench configurations, planning delegation captures a different reward–cost tradeoff from adding implementers or verifiers; inexpensive workers are not interchangeable across roles. This is a configured empirical result, not a general law that planning is always the best allocation. The study does not evaluate team safety. Its mechanism suggests a sharper ablation than team size alone: preserve the lead, budget and information access, vary the recipient stage, and measure integration work as well as worker output. A cheap planner can supply a useful alternative hypothesis while a cheap implementer creates edits the lead must repair. The relevant causal mediator is useful accepted work after integration, not the number of delegates or messages. Testing that mediator requires recording rejected plans, conflicting patches and redundant verification so hidden consolidation cost cannot be mistaken for free parallelism.

The integration step should be designed as carefully as worker execution. A manager receives candidate artifacts, validates their provenance, identifies disagreements, and chooses whether more work is justified. It should not simply concatenate worker summaries and ask another model to produce a fluent answer. Concatenation preserves text but does not resolve incompatible assumptions, duplicated evidence, or different interpretations of the task.

One useful protocol maintains a claim graph. Nodes are claims or artifact predicates; edges identify supporting evidence, contradiction, or dependency. Workers submit proposed graph updates rather than final conclusions alone. The manager checks whether two claims concern the same population, version, and resource envelope before labeling them contradictory. Apparent disagreement can disappear when one worker reports author results and another reports an independent reproduction under a different environment. Genuine unresolved disagreement should remain visible.

Integration can stop when all required predicates have accepted evidence, unresolved contradictions have been represented, and the remaining expected value of additional work is below its cost under the declared objective. This stopping rule is conceptual because value estimates are uncertain. An implementation can approximate it with bounded rounds, explicit missing-evidence categories, and a limit on repeated requests for the same information. The approximation should be evaluated rather than presented as optimal metareasoning.

The protocol also needs a quarantine path. A worker result containing unverifiable citations, unexplained external changes, or suspicious instructions should be retained for diagnosis without entering trusted shared memory. Quarantine is not deletion and does not itself prove maliciousness. It prevents uncertainty about one artifact from silently becoming authority for subsequent actions. False quarantines reduce useful throughput, so their rate belongs in the evaluation alongside successful containment.

For a scientific review task, integration should retain disagreements over contamination, baseline strength, and statistical uncertainty even when the final narrative would be simpler without them. For a coding task, it should retain a failing regression test rather than allow a worker’s confident explanation to supersede it. For enterprise actions, it should recheck authorization at the effect boundary. These examples share a principle: evidence and authority are properties of records and current policy, not consequences of a worker’s role label.

The resulting team is best understood as a controlled distribution of computation and evidence. Parallelism supplies opportunities for coverage and latency reduction. Typed handoffs preserve what each opportunity discovered. Shared-state protocols prevent those discoveries from becoming incoherent or unauthorized. Independent evaluation determines whether the arrangement improves useful outcomes. None of these layers can be omitted by appealing to the number of agents or the apparent sophistication of their conversation.

Consider two workers preparing changes to different modules of one repository. Their edits appear independent, but both modify a shared interface specification. A shared writable checkout permits immediate coordination through the filesystem, yet it also permits one worker to test a transient mixture of changes. The resulting passing test verdict may correspond to no committed artifact. A later merge can then fail despite both workers reporting success. This is an evidence-identity failure rather than a lack of programming ability.

An isolated-workspace design gives each worker a base revision and a separate branch. The manager merges their artifacts and runs integration checks on the merged digest. This adds storage and validation cost but creates a clear causal boundary: worker tests concern branch artifacts; integration tests concern the combined artifact. If the interface changes are incompatible, the conflict is explicit. Isolation does not prevent semantic incompatibility, but it prevents accidental shared state from concealing it.

The same reasoning applies to research. Two investigators can independently inspect conflicting papers before receiving each other’s conclusions. Their private notes preserve the evidence that motivated each interpretation. Discussion then operates on the disagreement rather than on an already homogenized summary. Complete isolation would prevent useful correction, so the design uses staged disclosure: independent extraction first, evidence exchange second, joint interpretation third. The stages allow an experiment to observe where agreement arises.

For memory systems, isolation can be temporary and selective. A worker may read a shared evidence snapshot while writing candidate interpretations to a private namespace. A promotion gate checks provenance, conflicts, and applicability before moving those interpretations into shared memory. This resembles a database transaction but adds semantic evaluation. The gate can still make mistakes, and its acceptance threshold determines the tradeoff between contamination and delayed learning. Promotion should therefore retain the original candidate and gate verdict for later audit.

The cost of this mechanism grows with candidate volume. If every worker proposes many redundant records, verification can dominate execution. Deduplication before promotion reduces load, but semantic deduplication can incorrectly merge distinct conditions. A safer first stage deduplicates exact source identities and artifact hashes; a later stage considers whether two interpretations are equivalent under their stated scope. Keeping these stages separate makes it possible to attribute errors to retrieval, deduplication, or review.

An evaluation should compare immediate shared writes, snapshot reads with private writes, and fully isolated memory under the same task sequence. Inject one incorrect but plausible record and measure its propagation, subsequent correction, and effect on task outcomes. Also include a valid rare record: a system that blocks all unusual memories may contain contamination while preventing beneficial transfer. Measure both harmful propagation and useful adoption, along with the review work needed to distinguish them.

The implication is conditional rather than categorical. Shared state is valuable when its information benefits exceed its coordination and contamination costs. Isolation is valuable when it preserves evidence identity, authority boundaries, or independent judgment. A principal design decision is to choose the smallest shared surface required for the task. Increasing communication and memory visibility without identifying the dependency they serve is not a scientific explanation of why a team should improve.
Figure isolates the mechanism and its stated information boundaries.

Workers can read one versioned snapshot while retaining candidate interpretations privately. Only the promotion path publishes accepted candidates into a new shared view; unresolved candidates remain separate. Provenance, conflict and applicability checks retain an auditable decision boundary. The gate does not establish semantic truth, current effect authority, or a performance improvement.

The October 2026 SDK releases expose failures that a framework comparison must represent. OpenAI Agents Python v0.24.0 defers automatic compaction while approvals are pending and preserves completed tool outputs when a sibling tool fails; Google ADK v2.13.0 marks its MongoDB session and memory services experimental . These are version-specific documented changes, not guarantees inferred from a brand. They motivate comparing the exact interruption, publication, and compatibility semantics of a framework before counting its integrations.

An agent framework is a set of choices about where control resides. Its most consequential properties are not the number of model adapters or the expressiveness of a demonstration, but the semantics of state, effects, interruption, authorization, and observation. A framework can make those semantics explicit, hide them behind convenience interfaces, or delegate them to another service. These alternatives impose different experimental and operational obligations.

The comparison in this chapter begins with role rather than rank. A graph runtime, a typed model SDK, an opinionated harness, a workflow builder, and a managed execution platform occupy different boundaries. They can compose within one application and should not be treated as mutually exclusive competitors. The official-source inventory is interpreted as documentation of interfaces available for inspection on the literature cutoff, not as an independently stress-tested feature leaderboard.

Define a framework profile by five sets: states it represents, transitions it controls, effects it mediates, observations it exports, and obligations it leaves to the application. This representation makes omissions visible. An SDK can validate a tool argument but leave external idempotency unspecified. A runtime can persist graph state but leave document authorization to a connector. A managed service can maintain sessions while exposing only partial execution traces. None of these limitations is inherently disqualifying; they determine the boundary of a defensible claim.

A useful comparison matrix distinguishes documented support from verified behavior. Persistence should be decomposed into conversation continuity, process-restart recovery, durable external artifacts, semantic memory, and cross-version migration. Human review should identify where execution pauses, what the reviewer sees, and whether authority is rechecked after resumption. Observability should identify whether traces include full tool arguments, truncation indicators, source identity, and asynchronous work. A single Boolean column loses these distinctions.

The unit of versioning is similarly broader than a package number. An application may combine a pinned SDK, moving model alias, remote tool schemas, hosted runtime, and changing connector permissions. Recording the SDK release alone does not reproduce the system. Define a compatibility vector whose components include each mutable boundary and attach it to evaluation traces. Unknown service revisions should remain unknown rather than be inferred from a documentation date.

More precisely, a configured deployment has a manifest : application/framework revision , model identity , deployment decoder , tool-schema/adapter revision , persistence backend/schema , and current authority epoch . These components need not share a release cycle. A saved run additionally requires its realized context and external-effect records; identifies configuration rather than reconstructing those data. Framework comparison holds the relevant components fixed or declares their joint change as the treatment. Otherwise a newer SDK coupled to a stronger model is not an estimate of an SDK effect.

For feature equivalence, require observable contracts. Two frameworks both exposing a method called resume are not equivalent if one restores a model-visible history and another resumes an event-sourced workflow. The first may repeat tool effects; the second may skip completed activities but depend on deterministic application code. A conformance workload should therefore include an interruption after external acceptance and before local commitment, rather than test only that a suspended conversation can receive another message.

The practical implication is to select a framework against the failure modes of the intended workload. A short extraction service may benefit most from typed output and dependency injection. A multi-hour engineering task needs workspace state, cancellation, and reconciliation. A regulated business action needs principal identity and authoritative permission checks. Breadth of advertised features cannot replace the task-specific evidence needed to compare these roles.

Graph runtimes make control flow an explicit application object. Nodes transform state, edges constrain possible continuations, and persistence attaches to defined execution boundaries. This can support inspection and fault recovery, but the graph is not automatically deterministic: nodes can contain model calls, time-dependent queries, or external effects. A graph’s visual clarity therefore does not prove replay equivalence. The implementation must identify which values are recorded and which computations execute again.

LangGraph illustrates a runtime layer, while Deep Agents supplies a more opinionated harness over that ecosystem . The latter’s documented filesystem, subagent, and context-management interfaces are mechanisms to examine. Their existence does not establish that summaries preserve every constraint or that delegated work is cheaper. A useful experiment holds the underlying runtime fixed and separately varies offloading, compaction, and delegation. Otherwise a comparison between the two layers confounds control defaults with the runtime itself.

An opinionated harness reduces application effort by choosing defaults for prompts, tools, memory, and stopping. The benefit is faster construction of a coherent system. The scientific cost is that a high-level configuration can activate several mechanisms at once. Researchers should expose these defaults in their experimental configuration and inspect the code path used by the evaluated task. Disabling a component should not silently activate a fallback whose cost or behavior is materially different.

Event-driven workflow systems provide another control model. Events describe completed work or new requirements, and handlers may schedule further tasks. This is useful when external processes, human decisions, or delayed data determine progress. However, event duplication and ordering become part of agent semantics. A workflow that processes the same approval event twice can execute an action twice unless it deduplicates by stable event identity. These concerns persist even if every model call is perfectly accurate.

The discriminating experiment is not whether a sample application runs. It is whether equivalent state transitions produce equivalent committed effects under interruptions, retries, and schema evolution. Use a small deterministic tool fixture first, then introduce model nondeterminism as a separate factor. This ordering prevents a transport or persistence defect from being misdiagnosed as reasoning failure. It also establishes which guarantees survive when the framework delegates execution to a managed backend.

Typed SDKs place schemas and application dependencies around model interactions. Type validation can reject malformed arguments, constrain output shape, and expose errors before application code executes. Its guarantee is syntactic and representational. A valid customer identifier can still refer to the wrong customer, and a well-typed monetary amount can still exceed authorization. Semantic preconditions must therefore remain explicit application checks rather than be assumed consequences of schema adherence.

The inspected OpenAI Agents SDK separates an application-owned SDK path from managed runtime options . Handoffs, tool loops, session interfaces, and tracing provide useful abstractions, but applications still own tool effects and their storage semantics. Its SDK is provider-agnostic; the evaluation must identify the selected model adapter rather than infer it from the SDK name . PydanticAI makes typed interaction an inspectable design surface and also supplies a configurable harness, while Pydantic Graph and Pydantic Evals are separate packages . Restricting its inventory to output validation would omit its current context, tool and execution controls. A comparison should examine how validation failures are surfaced, whether repair attempts consume the same budget, and whether rejected calls enter the trajectory used for later training or evaluation.

The Claude Agent SDK occupies a different ownership boundary from a Messages API client. Current official documentation describes a Python/TypeScript library running the Claude Code binary in an application-operated process, with its agent loop, tool execution, permissions, sessions and hooks. A client SDK instead exposes model requests, while Claude Managed Agents supplies a hosted harness with a separately configured execution environment . These are three distinct experimental treatments. A common model identifier does not make their context constructors or permission mechanisms equivalent.

One failure mode is repair-induced drift. A model proposes an invalid tool call, the SDK returns an error, and the next attempt changes a meaningful argument while correcting the format. If evaluation records only the final valid call, it omits the information that caused the transition. For a learned policy this can invalidate behavior-likelihood reconstruction. For a production service it can conceal repeated boundary probing. Validation and repair events should therefore be first-class trace records.

Model-owned loops choose their next action dynamically, whereas application-owned workflows constrain the available continuation structure. Neither is universally superior. Dynamic loops accommodate unforeseen subtasks but can cycle, invent unsupported tool names, or consume budgets without progress. Explicit workflows improve predictability but can fail when the task falls outside their branches. A hybrid design uses deterministic control for authority and commitment while permitting model-driven choice within a bounded action space.

The relevant baselines compare the same tool contract under direct function orchestration, a minimal agent loop, and the SDK’s higher-level abstractions. Measure invalid calls, repair rounds, constraint violations, total cost, and completion. A framework’s ergonomic advantage is real but requires a different study, such as developer implementation time under controlled tasks. It should not be inferred from task success or substituted for runtime reliability.

An agent development kit typically bundles authoring conventions, tool integration, orchestration, testing, and deployment adapters. This breadth can improve consistency but also creates version coupling. A task object serialized by one language implementation may not preserve every field expected by another. A model adapter can normalize errors differently, changing retry behavior. Cross-language support is therefore a compatibility question rather than a guarantee that all implementations have identical semantics.

Google ADK’s inspected repository describes graph-based workflows and structured delegation surfaces, while Microsoft Agent Framework describes multi-language agent and workflow construction . These are concrete interfaces for conformance tests. The experiment should pin the relevant implementation and compare equivalent task graphs, state updates, and failure injections. It should not compare unrelated examples and attribute the difference to the toolkit brand.

Protocol support is similarly conditional. A framework advertising MCP can expose tools, resources, or prompts through different transport and authorization configurations. An A2A integration can exchange task status without sharing the same memory model or trust boundary. Chapter treats these protocol distinctions directly. At the framework layer, the important question is which semantics are preserved when an adapter maps between local objects and external messages.

Serialization requires particular care for authority-bearing data. A human approval record should identify the precise operation, relevant arguments, principal, expiry, and policy epoch. Mapping it to an unstructured string in another framework weakens its meaning. The receiving application must validate the approval against its own action boundary. Successful message delivery cannot establish that the transferred object authorizes the requested effect.

Interoperability experiments should include a deliberate version mismatch, optional fields unknown to the receiver, partial tool failures, and revoked credentials. Report which failures are detected before dispatch and which emerge only after an effect. A graceful error is often preferable to a silent fallback that changes task meaning. The strongest interoperability result is a documented set of preserved invariants under declared adapters, not an assertion that any agent can collaborate safely with any other.

Table assigns each listed framework or managed runtime a concrete inspection target. The entries describe documentation surfaces, not measured capability or comparative quality. The final column is a discriminating test: it identifies an observation needed before an engineering conclusion is justified. Where a source redirects, the resolved resource defines the inspected family; historical names are lineage identifiers. Package and hosted-service parity remain unverified unless established by a version-specific test.

Several entries cross category boundaries. Pi can be used as a coding harness and as an extension substrate. NeMo Fabric concerns execution and telemetry across harnesses rather than a replacement for the model policy. DSPy concerns program and prompt optimization against evaluation objectives; it should be tested for selection overfitting as well as task quality. A visual builder such as Langflow, Dify, Coze Studio, or n8n can host model-driven steps inside deterministic workflows. Its graphical interface does not remove the need to examine stored state, credential scope, and replay behavior.

Managed platforms change the observation boundary. AgentCore, Agent Bricks, and Google’s enterprise platform document infrastructure surfaces that an application can compose with custom agents. Managed agent APIs supply a larger portion of the loop. These roles should be compared through migration effort, observability, failure recovery, and enforceable policy controls, rather than counted as additional reasoning architectures. A serverless runtime’s availability commitment is not evidence that an agent’s task output is correct.

Implementation visibility, artifact license, hosted-service terms, and operational inspectability are separate properties. A public repository can contain a client while the service remains proprietary. A source-visible license can restrict deployment or redistribution. A permissive core license may coexist with separately licensed connectors or enterprise features. The defensible statement identifies the inspected artifact and its license file at a revision; it does not attach an unqualified open-source label to an entire product family.

The inspected repository notices illustrate why this granularity matters. Mastra distinguishes its Apache-2.0 core from enterprise-licensed directories; n8n identifies Sustainable Use and Enterprise licenses; Dify identifies an Apache-2.0-derived license with additional conditions . These notices establish artifact-specific terms, not a universal compatibility judgment between deployments. DeepSeek Harness explicitly declares developer-preview status and anticipated compatibility-breaking changes . An active commit stream therefore does not establish a stable serialized-state or plugin ABI.

Lifecycle changes can invalidate comparisons even when names remain familiar. The inspected Llama Stack link resolves into the OGX lineage, and the Llama workflow link resolves to a broader agents repository. The Strands source link resolves to a harness SDK resource. These redirects are evidence of naming and packaging changes, not proof of complete backward compatibility. An application relying on old imports, storage schemas, or tool names needs a migration test rather than a renamed bibliography entry.

Historical products should be preserved where they explain architectural evolution, but they should not be described as active recommendations without current evidence. Archive status, maintenance activity, security-fix policy, and availability are distinct. A repository can remain readable after service termination; a commercial service can remain available while a legacy SDK is deprecated. The operating consequence is to maintain a dependency inventory with replacement and rollback plans, particularly for long-lived memory formats.

A migration experiment starts from a saved run and its authoritative state. Restore under the target release, validate schemas, rebuild indexes when required, and replay deterministic fixtures before permitting new model decisions. Compare tool availability, parser behavior, serialization, and cancellation. A test that merely imports the new package misses the semantics most likely to affect agent behavior. If the provider does not expose the necessary version controls, report that reproducibility limitation explicitly.

For a deterministic fixture, write for a release’s state transition and for its observable event output. Let be a partial migration with the same fixture inputs . On a transition-closed migration domain, require

If both identities hold for every admitted , induction on the finite input sequence gives identical fixture event traces and corresponding states after every step. This is a contract-preservation criterion, not a claim that all migrations satisfy it. The event space must include relevant tool intents, validation failures and recorded receipts; comparing only final chat strings discards precisely the events that can change effects. Real remote effects still require the service contract of Chapter . A migration may legitimately reject an unsupported saved state; silently coercing it into another agent’s state violates the criterion. A finite test suite provides evidence on its reached states, not proof of the universal identities. Stochastic model transitions require distributional comparison or fixed recorded outputs, rather than assuming identical samples.

Ownership and acquisition claims are excluded from technical inference unless primary evidence establishes them and they matter to the system boundary. Even a verified corporate change does not imply that products share code, data, or runtime guarantees. The analysis follows inspectable mechanisms and contracts. This avoids turning a provider map into an unsupported architectural map.

The official release records rechecked on 29 October identify LangGraph 1.2.18 on 26 October 2026, OpenAI Agents Python SDK 0.24.0 on 15 October, Google ADK 2.13.0 published on 23 October with release-note heading dated 22 October, and PydanticAI 2.63.0 on 28 October . These identifiers delimit the evidence; a current main branch can contain later or unreleased changes. Microsoft’s repository has distinct .NET 1.26.0 and Python 1.23.0 releases, dated 23 and 22 October respectively, rather than one universal cross-language release . CrewAI’s inspected release was 1.15.32, while smolagents’ latest returned release was 1.26.0 from May . Release recency alone is not a quality metric.

Several changes directly affect the consistency arguments in this book. LangGraph’s notes change the default frequency of full delta snapshots from one thousand updates to one hundred, trading additional storage for faster reads on long threads. This is a concrete checkpoint-layout change, not evidence of better semantic memory. The Agents SDK notes defer automatic compaction during pending approvals, replace Redis compaction history atomically, and preserve completed tool outputs when a sibling fails. Those fixes identify distinct state boundaries: approval evidence, history replacement and partial parallel completion. They motivate targeted regression fixtures rather than a general claim that all consistency problems are solved .

ADK’s release notes mark MongoDB session and memory services experimental even while promoting other features to stable status. They also change the default telemetry schema. Consequently, neither maturity nor trace compatibility should be assigned at whole-framework granularity. An analytics pipeline that assumes an older span layout can silently lose attribution after an otherwise successful upgrade. PydanticAI’s notes change the default of its CodeMode dynamic catalog so newly revealed tools append rather than rewrite cached prompts. That is a component-specific context-construction choice whose effect depends on tool-discovery workload and cache behavior; it is not a universal change to every tool path or a measured application-level speedup .

A deterministic migration criterion compares the two paths through corresponding fixture states. On an admitted transition-closed domain, migration must commute with the state transition and preserve the declared observable events. Finite fixtures test reached states; they do not prove the universal identities or establish remote-effect uniqueness.

A framework conformance suite should exercise schema validation, state restoration, duplicate dispatch, cancellation, authorization revocation, and trace completeness before comparing task scores. Each fixture has an expected observable contract. For example, a revoked write capability must prevent a new effect even if an old checkpoint contains a permission statement. A committed terminal receipt should be replayed without a new effect; an unresolved dispatch should reconcile before any retry justified by the service’s explicit retry contract. A truncated tool result should carry an explicit truncation indication or preserve a recoverable artifact reference.

Conformance is not a universal safety certificate. It establishes behavior for the tested contract and release. A framework can pass deterministic fixtures and still induce poor model decisions through context construction. Therefore the second stage evaluates task outcomes under matched models, tools, and budgets. Separate the effect of the framework from the effect of its recommended prompt, default model, and hosted extensions. When those cannot be separated, the treatment is the complete configured system.

Component effects need not be additive. For two configurable mechanisms, let be expected task outcome when mechanism one has state and mechanism two has state , with the backbone, information access, resource envelope and task population fixed. The interaction is

For example, compaction can change which tool descriptions remain visible, while dynamic discovery changes which descriptions need to survive compaction. A gain from enabling both does not identify either individual contribution; a nonzero measures their departure from additivity on the declared outcome scale. If an SDK cannot expose all four configurations, the interaction is unidentified from that product comparison. This is an explicit observation limit, not a reason to assign the combined gain to the most prominently advertised feature.

Statistical comparisons should use paired tasks and report uncertainty at the task or session level. Framework adapters can fail only on particular tool schemas, so stratify by schema complexity and effect type. Count startup failures, missing outputs, and dependency outages rather than removing them as setup problems after observing results. A system that requires undocumented manual repair has a materially different operational profile from one that completes unattended under the same fixtures.

Finally, include an implementation-complexity analysis without mistaking it for benchmark quality. Count application-owned components, external dependencies, state stores, custom adapters, and recovery code. These counts do not form a universal simplicity score, but they explain where maintenance responsibility resides. A highly capable managed service may reduce local code while increasing opaque dependencies. A minimal SDK may expose more work but permit a stronger audit. The appropriate choice depends on which uncertainty the deployment can tolerate and which guarantees it must enforce.

A concrete audit can start with three interfaces rather than an entire framework taxonomy. In the inspected LangGraph source tree, the state-graph implementation resides in the graph state module and exposes compilation into an executable graph. In the OpenAI Agents Python SDK, the run module exposes the Runner control surface. The Google ADK source exposes runner infrastructure for application execution. These are identifiable inspection points, not assertions that the corresponding modules implement every guarantee discussed above. Their current source files were reachable at the cutoff; experiment revisions still require immutable pinning .

For the graph case, trace compilation into checkpoint use. Identify where thread identity enters configuration, which state updates are reduced together, and which node outputs are persisted before successors execute. Then place an effectful tool call inside one node and inject a crash immediately after the service accepts it. If resumption reexecutes the node, the application must supply idempotency or reconciliation. This test distinguishes graph-state durability from external-effect uniqueness without requiring a language model in the fixture.

For the Runner case, trace model output through tool-call decoding, schema validation, execution, and subsequent model input. Capture the exact error object returned for an invalid argument. Then inspect whether a handoff changes the active instructions, tools, model settings, or state ownership. The experiment should preserve the pre-handoff authority envelope and verify that delegation cannot expand it. A handoff that routes a conversation successfully can still be incorrect if it transfers more context or credentials than the receiving specialist requires.

Current source inspection supplies narrower testable claims. LangGraph’s pinned DeltaChannel constructor sets snapshot_frequency=100; this supports the checkpoint-layout claim without asserting semantic preservation by compaction . The Agents SDK’s pinned RunState uses schema 1.21 and rejects ambiguous legacy agent identities; its documentation warns that neither context overrides nor strict context deserialization establishes snapshot integrity . The required fixture therefore changes a duplicate-agent graph and verifies a safe rejection, rather than relabeling an old checkpoint until loading succeeds. Serialization compatibility and authenticity are separate checks.

For an ADK application, inspect how an event updates session state and how workflow execution consumes that state. Duplicate one event identifier and delay another. The expected behavior must come from the selected application’s contract, because a generic toolkit may legitimately expose several scheduling modes. Evaluate whether the serialized event contains sufficient identity to diagnose the difference. A toolkit’s flexibility increases the number of legal configurations; it does not eliminate the need to state which one produced a result.

For example, the pinned ADK InMemorySessionService.append_event skips partial events and suppresses an equal re-delivery only after matching its event identifier. Distinct event objects with the same identifier but different fields are retained. Its scope is an in-memory session implementation, not restart durability or universal event-ID uniqueness across backends . A discriminating fixture must therefore test both identical re-delivery and conflicting reuse, and must inspect the selected persistent backend independently. An identifier’s presence in a serialized object is insufficient evidence that every consumer enforces its intended uniqueness.

These inspections produce a claim-to-code ledger. Each row records the public claim, source revision, module and callable, relevant configuration, injected condition, expected invariant, and observed outcome. Until the fixture has run, the outcome field remains unmeasured. This restraint prevents source inspection from becoming an invented reproduction. When the experiment does run, a discrepancy should lead to a narrower conclusion: perhaps a configured checkpointer preserves local state, while the selected tool adapter repeats effects. Blaming or endorsing the entire framework would discard the evidence about where the behavior actually arose.

The ledger also identifies work needed for upgrades. If a release changes the callable responsible for event reduction or tool retries, rerun the fixtures attached to those claims. An unrelated documentation edit need not trigger all experiments. This dependency-based approach makes validation scalable while retaining scientific traceability. It is especially useful for agent systems because a small change to error serialization can alter the model’s next action even when the application’s visible API remains compatible.

TestJack’s October 2026 audit constructs prompt-grounded witness tests against candidates that passed existing coding evaluators; AgentHorizon separately examines computer-use evaluation with task instructions and execution trajectories . Both cases challenge the inference from a favorable grader response to completed work. They expose different observation gaps: a test suite may omit a stated requirement, while an interface snapshot may omit the action history needed to interpret the final state. Neither audit provides an infallible judge.

Coding agents operate on artifacts whose correctness is partly executable, but executable does not mean fully specified. A patch can satisfy the visible tests while violating a stated requirement that those tests omit, introducing a security regression, or modifying the tests themselves. An underspecified requirement instead needs adjudication before disagreement can refute the patch. Computer-use agents add another observation problem: a screenshot can show a plausible final state without proving that the requested object, recipient, or permission was selected. The shared objective is to connect task interpretation, environment interaction, and independently checkable evidence.

The central comparison is between complete configured systems. Model, harness, repository context, tool interface, execution environment, evaluator, and budget all influence results. Product names are insufficient experimental identifiers. This chapter analyzes these boundaries, gives concrete implementation and benchmark anchors, and distinguishes inspectable mechanisms from undocumented hosted behavior.

A repository task is a partially observed transition problem. The agent observes selected files, search results, test outputs, and version-control metadata. It acts through edits, commands, dependency operations, and sometimes remote services. The true environment includes build tools, generated files, network dependencies, and hidden tests that may not appear in its initial context. Treating the task as text completion discards the execution feedback that makes repository-level work distinctive.

The action interface should preserve artifact identity. A patch request names its base revision and intended file changes; command execution records working directory, environment, exit status, and captured output. The test verdict binds to the resulting artifact digest. If the agent edits code after testing, the verdict must be invalidated or rerun. This mechanical correspondence is separate from whether the tests capture the intended behavior.

An execution attestation can make that boundary explicit. Let be the tested artifact, its declared dependency/environment manifest, and record their digests, the exact test invocation , exit status , and execution trace . With denoting a complete, attributable invocation record, define

This predicate establishes provenance of a zero-exit execution for the declared inputs, assuming collision-resistant hashing and trustworthy records. It does not establish requirement coverage, authentic dependencies beyond the captured manifest, or absence of unrecorded network/environment changes. A failed command followed by a persuasive final message has ; an edit after testing changes and invalidates the old attestation. Test discovery failures and a command that executes no relevant tests still require separate validation even when its exit status is zero.

The 2024 SWE-agent study established an influential interface baseline and demonstrates the importance of the agent-computer interface rather than model capability alone . Search, file navigation, editing, and error feedback change how effectively the model can act on repository state. The proper inference is interface sensitivity in the studied setting. It does not establish that one interface dominates across languages, repositories, models, and tool latency. A useful replication preserves the evaluator and workload while varying only the interaction surface.

The implementation anchor is an actual rollout through the published repository: model input construction, command interface, environment stepping, output truncation, and termination. A researcher should locate the callable that executes actions and the adapter that converts its results back into model-visible messages. Silent truncation or error normalization can materially change the policy. Comparing only prompt templates misses those mechanisms.

Repository isolation also matters. An agent should not see another benchmark task’s generated artifacts or hidden test outcomes through a shared checkout or cache. The workspace, dependencies, and stateful tools need a reset policy. Reusing a build cache may be legitimate for cost analysis but must not transfer answer-bearing files across tasks. Separate a warm infrastructure cache from persistent semantic memory and report both explicitly.
Figure isolates the mechanism and its stated information boundaries.

The same execution record is checked against two artifact revisions. It binds to the tested artifact in the left panel; the illustrated edit changes the digest and invalidates that binding in the right panel. Matching provenance identifies the object tested, while requirement coverage, the declared environment and current authority need their own checks.

Let be the intended requirement set and the executable test set. Passing supports correctness only for the behaviors it covers under the tested environment. It does not imply satisfaction of every element of . The gap can arise from missing tests, ambiguous requirements, faulty reference solutions, nondeterministic infrastructure, or a grader that observes the wrong artifact.

A verification gate therefore needs two error rates: false acceptance of a defective artifact and false rejection of a valid artifact. Both depend on the distribution of candidate patches. An evaluator calibrated on ordinary human patches may behave differently on agent-generated solutions that exploit unusual shortcuts. Adaptive optimization against the same visible tests increases this risk because the agent can learn the evaluator’s blind spots rather than the task’s intended semantics.

For a declared candidate population, let denote requirement correctness after adjudication and the grader’s acceptance. Write , , , and , assuming both correctness classes have positive probability. The law of total probability gives

Thus accepted fraction is not identified with correct fraction. If , this grader’s acceptance carries no information about correctness prevalence in that population. The same decomposition yields . These are population identities, not a correction obtained by importing a false-acceptance rate from a different benchmark. Estimation requires an independently adjudicated sample of the same candidate process, with uncertainty propagated jointly through ; a small makes inversion unstable. Changing agents, search budgets or visible-test exposure can change both conditional error rates. Stress fixtures establish sensitivity to their seeded defects and need not estimate the natural population rates.

SWE-Bench Pro increases task complexity and uses public, held-out, and commercial repository groups . Its access structure is important evidence about reproducibility: independently auditing public tasks is not equivalent to reproducing results on unavailable proprietary tasks. A contamination-resistant design also does not prove absence of prior exposure. The survey should preserve those distinctions when comparing numbers across benchmark versions and scaffolds.

A concrete failure case is a patch that handles the sample input but fails on a boundary condition implied by the specification. Another modifies a serialization path correctly while breaking a related caller absent from the visible tests. A third passes locally but depends on an undeclared environment variable. These cases require different interventions: requirement-derived tests, integration coverage, and environment capture. More chain-of-thought tokens do not directly repair an evaluator that never checks the failing behavior.

Reference implementations are useful but fallible. A differential test that distinguishes a candidate from a reference detects disagreement; it establishes a defect only if the reference behavior follows the requirement. Human or model interpretation of that requirement can still err. Report the adjudication procedure and unresolved ambiguity rather than treating reference agreement as mathematical truth. Chapter develops this verification boundary further.

Terminal agents expose a broad action space through a compact interface. The same shell can inspect files, run tests, modify dependencies, and invoke network tools. This flexibility reduces the number of specialized APIs needed, but it makes semantic validation harder. A syntactically valid command can have effects far beyond the intended task. The sandbox and permission layer must mediate those effects independently of the model’s stated intent.

Long terminal trajectories contain more than command examples. They include evidence gathering, hypothesis revision, failed attempts, recovery, and final artifact validation. TerminalHorizon explicitly studies synthesis of task environments that preserve the work needed for these behaviors . Its environment-reconstruction mechanism is relevant because a synthetic setup can accidentally solve the difficult part before the agent begins. A training example then rewards superficial completion rather than the intended exploration.

The current v2 separates a task package into public instruction and environment and private reference solution, verifier and construction configuration. Its independent challenger is uninvolved in construction and solves from the public interface; trace-based diagnosis then guides reconstruction of work accidentally simplified during setup. Progressive expansion adds requirements under the same goal that depend on earlier results and feedback . This is more specific than increasing a maximum turn count. Challenger success alone does not certify absence of every shortcut, and generated verifier agreement remains conditional on its task specification. The appropriate ablation changes reconstruction or expansion separately while preserving model, training tokens and evaluation access, and reports both task coverage and the work demonstrably left for the learner.

The causal comparison should distinguish richer trajectories from easier environments. Keep initial information, required work, and evaluator access comparable across data-generation variants. Audit whether task descriptions leak a solution, whether setup scripts precompute key artifacts, and whether generated tests reveal hidden requirements. Supervised fine-tuning gains on multiple benchmarks can be informative while leaving these construction confounds unresolved.

Trajectory learning also depends on actual behavior conditioning. If a training pipeline reconstructs context after the fact and removes information the policy originally saw, logged actions no longer correspond to the assumed policy inputs. MemoryWalker addresses this class of mismatch . For coding agents, record context edits, tool-output truncation, and environment version along with actions. A repository checkout and final patch are insufficient to reconstruct the decision process.

Evaluation should report progress through the full task rather than command validity alone. Measure artifact success, constraints, execution cost, recovery, and whether the final output identifies tested and untested behavior. A terminal agent that produces a plausible explanation after failing to run tests should not receive the same completion status as one with verified results. Conversely, an infrastructure outage should remain visible as an environmental failure rather than be silently removed from the denominator.

The inspected mini-swe-agent release 2.4.6, dated 23 July 2026, explicitly counts billed calls that fail parsing against the cost limit . This small implementation detail materially changes budget-matched evaluation: excluding paid malformed responses would give a system additional effective resources while reporting the same nominal limit. It is a concrete example of why a minimal loop remains useful as a research baseline but still requires release-level inspection. The relevant experiment compares identical malformed-output schedules before and after the accounting change, measuring budget overshoot and completed work rather than inferring a reasoning improvement from the release note.

The pinned implementation confirms a further boundary. DefaultAgent.query checks already accumulated cost before the next model call; successful calls add returned cost, while the FormatError recovery branch adds reported billed cost from the exception record . This is post-charge accounting, not the reservation protocol of Chapter . For one serial query loop, assume admission and cost updates are serialized, at most one charge remains unrecorded in flight, and each charge is recorded before admitting the next call. If is the active threshold, the initial total is below , and each newly admitted call costs at most , the pre-call check bounds the charged total by , rather than by . Parallel callers can all pass a stale total, so the one-call bound is not a global concurrency guarantee. Without a known call-cost ceiling there is no finite overshoot bound from that check alone. Tool fees and environment charges outside this counter require separate accounting. A reproducible budget comparison must therefore distinguish a declared stopping threshold from a guaranteed maximum expenditure.

Computer-use agents act through visual observations and input events. The policy must connect screen coordinates or semantic targets to application state, often across scrolling, asynchronous updates, and multiple windows. A click can be delivered successfully to the wrong object. Therefore transport acknowledgment and task correctness are especially far apart. The environment should record both intended target and observed result where the interface permits it.

Coordinate systems require explicit transformations. Let be a point in the image presented to the model, its letterbox offset, the rendered content dimensions, and the corresponding crop dimensions in physical screenshot pixels. If is the crop offset inside a screenshot whose desktop origin is , the adapter must apply

The expression assumes axis-aligned resizing without rotation and one physical-pixel coordinate system; CSS coordinates or device-independent units require an additional declared transform. Points outside the content rectangle should be rejected rather than clamped onto an unintended control. A deterministic mapping defect can dominate performance while being misdiagnosed as poor visual reasoning. Tests should perturb resolution, crop, letterboxing, viewport and display scaling independently. Even a correct map becomes stale if the application moves the target between observation and dispatch, so the observation identity and permitted delay remain part of the action contract.
