Let , suppose the model-space localization error is at most , and bound the remaining calibration residual on the relevant image region by . During delay , assume the target region undergoes only a rigid translation of norm at most . If the intended desktop point has interior margin to the target’s complement at observation time, then

ensures the dispatched point remains inside the translated target region: the triangle inequality bounds its displacement relative to that region by the left-hand side. This is an analytical interface condition, not an estimated guarantee for a vision model. Reflow, disappearance, occlusion, disabled controls, focus changes and a wrong semantic target invalidate or fall outside the hypotheses. Even an inside-region click still requires outcome verification. The condition explains why timestamped observations, calibration tests and a new screenshot after layout changes can address distinct failure mechanisms.

Screenshots are incomplete observations. They may omit hidden cells, collapsed panels, off-screen recipients, background downloads, or permission dialogs. A final screenshot showing a document title does not establish that the document contains the required data. Agents need application-specific verification or additional observations. When APIs are available, they can provide stronger state evidence, but the evaluation must declare whether the agent or only the evaluator can use them.

AgentHorizon evaluates judges on instruction-trajectory pairs, including closely related instructions whose trajectories are not interchangeable . This paired design exposes a common failure: accepting a trajectory because it looks like successful work while missing a constraint that distinguishes the actual request. The result concerns judge reliability, not merely executor capability. It motivates storing sufficient history for verification while also testing whether a judge can locate the relevant evidence.

An experiment should separate perception, target selection, action delivery, and outcome verification. Oracle target coordinates quantify perception headroom; replayed actions quantify environment determinism; authoritative state checks audit the final judge. The oracle conditions are diagnostic controls, not deployable capabilities. Report how much each stage contributes to failure and how those contributions change with task horizon. A single end-to-end score cannot identify which interface should be improved.

Table places coding, terminal, editor, and application-building systems into one comparison program without treating them as equivalent. A product may span local and remote execution, and an exposed client does not make its entire service inspectable. The official surfaces were rechecked on 29 October 2026; experimental claims require the corresponding executable configuration and evidence. Retrieval failure on a product homepage is not a capability verdict: Lovable’s official documentation establishes its application-building and code-export surfaces, while the resolved Antigravity 2.0 announcement distinguishes a standalone agent application from its separate IDE .

The important mechanisms cut across these families. Editor integration can reduce navigation cost and expose project context, but it can also hide unsaved state or privileged extensions. Cloud delegation can provide isolated environments and parallel work, but adds environment reconstruction and artifact-transfer boundaries. Application builders can integrate deployment tightly, but task success must then include the deployed artifact and its operational configuration rather than only a generated preview.

Codex’s documented SDK and open harness interfaces provide concrete inspection boundaries, while its hosted application and services remain separate components . Claude Code’s public repository and SDK documentation likewise require artifact-specific interpretation . No claim of complete implementation visibility follows from a public issue tracker or client repository. For both families, experiments must identify what runs locally, what runs remotely, and where state and authority are enforced.

The current inventory also contains consequential context-lifecycle distinctions. Letta Code’s pinned README describes memory, skills, prompts and harness modifications as adaptation surfaces; its cloud backend manages bundled default prompts on resume unless the documented preservation option is selected. That is a configuration transition requiring capture, not evidence of a fixed policy or autonomous weight improvement . Qwen Code exposes multiple provider protocols and SDK/desktop/browser interfaces, so treating every Qwen Code run as one Qwen model is incorrect . Tabnine’s OpenCode distribution supplies its own managed binary, Tabnine-served model selection and organization controls; sharing an underlying agent family does not establish equivalence to a separately configured OpenCode installation . Provider lineage and product packaging must remain distinct from the manifest of an evaluated run.

In the pinned Codex TypeScript SDK, CodexExec.run spawns the CLI with a JSON event stream, and Thread.run reduces completed-item events into a buffered return value. A turn-failure event causes that buffered path to throw; completed items accumulated earlier are not returned as a successful Turn. The streaming path exposes events as they arrive . An application needing partial-progress recovery should durably record relevant events and artifact identities while streaming, rather than infer that a thrown turn produced no work. Neither stream persistence nor a completed-item event by itself certifies the absence of unresolved remote effects. This is a source-level distinction between event delivery and task completion, not an independently measured failure rate.

The evaluation unit is a task plus initial environment, permitted resources, and scoring contract. Pin repository commit, dependency state, tool versions, model identity where available, and product configuration. If a hosted product does not expose a stable model or harness revision, record the retrieval and execution dates and restrict conclusions to the observed service. A nominally repeated experiment can change when the provider updates an opaque component.

Use task-level paired comparisons. Each system receives the same problem and a reset environment, with task order randomized where persistent memory is enabled. Declare whether memory may transfer between repositories or projects. A system with privileged workspace history has a different information budget from a fresh baseline. This difference may be a legitimate deployment advantage, but it must not be misrepresented as an intrinsic model gain.

Resource accounting includes input and output tokens, tool fees, environment startup, waiting, retries, verifier work, and human intervention. Report elapsed time and monetary cost separately. A cloud product can exploit parallel resources unavailable to a local baseline; matching elapsed time alone then compares different total compute. Conversely, matching dollars may permit different wall-clock and environment availability. The comparison axes should precede any ranking.

Ablations should target interfaces as well as prompts. Compare full repository search with restricted retrieval, executable feedback with model-only critique, persistent workspace with fresh workspace, and independent samples with coordinated subagents. Preserve test access and scoring across conditions. Where a product does not permit a component ablation, report the complete configured treatment rather than inventing an internal causal explanation.

Failure analysis should retain invalid calls, unexecuted tests, timeouts, partial patches, and inaccessible tasks. Distinguish infrastructure failures from policy errors without removing either from overall operational reliability. Confidence intervals should cluster repeated attempts by task and repository where applicable. If the sample is too small to distinguish adjacent products, report that uncertainty rather than converting a noisy ordering into a purchasing recommendation.

A coding agent’s final message should identify the artifact, the checks actually executed, their outcomes, and material limitations. This is not merely presentation quality. It gives the recipient the evidence needed to distinguish a proposed solution from a validated change. A confident statement that tests pass is not evidence if the trace records a skipped or failed command. The harness should generate factual execution status from authoritative records whenever possible.

Reviewable completion requires a stable artifact boundary. In version control, that can be a commit digest or patch against a known base. In a browser-created application, it can be an exported bundle and deployment identifier. In a computer-use task, it can be an authoritative application record with its permission state. The boundary varies, but it must allow the verifier to inspect the same object the agent claims to have completed.

Human review is an additional control, not an oracle. Reviewers have limited time, may anchor on the agent’s explanation, and may not inspect every dependency or generated file. The agent should therefore expose high-risk changes and missing evidence rather than bury them in a long narrative. Evaluation can measure whether reviewers detect seeded defects under a fixed review budget. It should not claim safety merely because a workflow contains an approval button.

The strongest engineering design binds authority to the transition being approved. Approval of a patch does not authorize later unrelated edits; approval to prepare a deployment does not necessarily authorize publication. If the artifact changes after review, the approval’s dependency digest should fail validation. A resumed session must recheck current permissions even if its history contains an earlier grant. These conditions connect coding agents to the broader authorization analysis of Chapter .

The practical conclusion is that coding and computer-use competence is a property of an evidence-producing execution system. Better models expand what can be attempted. Better interfaces reduce avoidable friction. Stronger evaluators identify a larger subset of defects. Durable state and authority checks keep long tasks coherent. Each layer has an identifiable contribution and a residual failure surface. Scientific comparison requires preserving those layers rather than attributing every successful artifact to an undifferentiated agent product.

Consider a task requiring a report to be saved in a particular project folder without changing its sharing settings. A computer-use trajectory creates a report with the correct title and visible content, but saves it in a similarly named personal folder. A judge that examines only the final screenshot may accept it. The error is not necessarily poor visual recognition: the relevant distinction may be absent from that screenshot. A stronger model given the same incomplete evidence cannot reliably infer the missing location.

The first control supplies an authoritative folder identifier to the judge while leaving the executor unchanged. If acceptance errors disappear, the observation interface is implicated. The second control provides the full trajectory, including the save dialog, but no authoritative identifier. This tests whether historical evidence is sufficient and whether the judge can retrieve it. The third swaps the instruction for a closely related request that would be satisfied by the observed trajectory. This tests whether the judge checks instruction-specific constraints rather than rewarding generic task plausibility. AgentHorizon’s paired instruction design directly motivates this distinction .

An analogous repository failure occurs when an agent changes a public function’s return format while preserving the sample command’s output. Unit tests focused on the sample pass, but a downstream caller breaks. Supplying more model-generated critique may or may not find the defect. A requirement-derived integration test provides a different kind of evidence because it executes the affected contract. Yet the test can still be wrong if it encodes an interpretation not required by the task. The evaluation must therefore retain both the executable failure and its requirement justification.

Causal diagnosis records the full execution and scoring chain. The task contains a constraint; the executor either overlooks it or lacks an adequate observation; the artifact violates it; the grader fails to inspect the decisive evidence; the final score reports success. Intervening only on the last step corrects the benchmark label but does not improve the executor. Intervening on the executor can improve artifacts while leaving the grader vulnerable to future failure classes. These are separate research contributions and should not share one undifferentiated reliability claim.

The implementation ledger for this case identifies the task adapter, initial state constructor, action executor, trace serializer, grader input builder, and acceptance function. At each boundary, record whether the decisive folder identifier or function contract remains available. A missing field is a concrete engineering finding. A present field ignored by the judge is a model or prompting finding. A correct judge verdict overwritten by a scoring adapter is an evaluation implementation finding. Locating the boundary prevents expensive model changes from being used to compensate for a deterministic data-loss defect.

The proposed experiment reports false acceptance, false rejection, evidence sufficiency, and evaluator cost under each control. Tasks are paired by instruction family, so uncertainty must preserve that pairing. Seeded defects help establish diagnostic sensitivity but do not estimate their natural deployment prevalence. Real trajectory audits complement them by identifying failures the fixture designer did not anticipate. The combination supplies a stronger basis for improvement than either a large leaderboard score or a handful of impressive demonstrations.

Deployment also requires a distributional statement. Folder-confusion fixtures test sensitivity to deliberately ambiguous names rather than overall product quality. A low frequency in a small natural sample does not exclude the failure. Combine stress-test sensitivity with an uncertain estimate of deployment exposure. When an error changes permissions or publishes an artifact, its tail consequence can dominate despite high average completion.

The 2026 Knowledge Activation study and ALE locate two different evidence boundaries. The former reports engineers’ perceived benefits in a particular organizational study; the latter constructs professional task evaluations whose measured outcomes do not directly identify enterprise productivity or economy-wide value . Treating either as proof that a named product improves every knowledge workflow would exceed its design. This chapter uses those boundaries to connect source-grounded research, permissioned business effects, memory services, and the deployment experiments required to establish value.

Research and enterprise agents share an evidence problem but differ in what their outputs authorize. A research agent must connect conclusions to sources and preserve unresolved disagreement. An enterprise agent may use those conclusions to change a customer record, create a legal work product, or trigger a business process. The latter adds identity, permissions, transactional effects, and organizational accountability. A fluent report is insufficient evidence for either role, and a well-grounded report does not automatically authorize the actions it recommends.

The objective of this chapter is a role-based account of these systems, including memory services that supply their context. Product documentation identifies integration and execution surfaces available for inspection; it does not establish scientific validity, deployment benefit, or universal capability. The analysis therefore connects each family to a concrete failure mechanism and a discriminating evaluation.

A research workflow contains query construction, source acquisition, identity resolution, claim extraction, comparison, synthesis, and revision. Each stage can fail independently. A source can be relevant but outdated, a claim can be extracted accurately but applied to the wrong population, or a synthesis can cite a paper that never measured the asserted outcome. Counting citations or generated pages does not distinguish these errors.

Represent a claim as a tuple containing proposition, scope, evidence class, source version, result location, assumptions, and unresolved limitations. An evidence graph links claims to supporting or contradicting observations. This representation makes revision possible: if a paper changes its result, the system can identify dependent conclusions rather than rewrite every paragraph blindly. It also separates author-reported evidence from independent reproduction and analytical deduction.

The query policy should seek disconfirming evidence as well as support. A system rewarded for completing a coherent report can stop after finding sources that fit its initial hypothesis. A better evaluation includes questions where the decisive result is negative, where two studies use incompatible definitions, or where the available implementation cannot substantiate a headline claim. The correct output may be a narrower conclusion or an explicit unresolved state rather than a more confident answer.

Hosted research products and inspectable research harnesses occupy different reproducibility boundaries. DeerFlow exposes a research-oriented harness, while Asta’s public resources distinguish research implementations from the hosted service . Consequently, a result obtained with a published baseline cannot be attributed to every hosted variant, and a hosted demonstration does not reproduce the baseline. Evaluation must name the actual execution path and available tools.

The stopping condition is evidence sufficiency under a declared question, not exhaustion of a token budget or attainment of a target report length. An implementation can maintain unresolved claim categories and a bounded search frontier. It should report whether searches failed because no qualifying evidence was found, because a source was inaccessible, or because the budget ended. These states have different scientific implications and should not collapse into a single statement that evidence is absent.

The October 2026 biological frontier spans several distinct control loops. Paper2Agent converts papers and associated code into MCP interfaces and checks their executable behavior; its September Nature article demonstrates genomic and transcriptomic cases while retaining human responsibility for open-ended interpretation . WetRobo’s September report instead studies coding-agent adaptation of a laboratory robot kit on three equipment-manipulation tasks, including bottle-cap transfer between two laboratories . Neither result alone establishes autonomous experimental discovery: method execution, equipment manipulation, scientific interpretation and selection of new experiments are different tasks with different ground truth.

This distinction determines what memory should retain. Reusing a numerical analysis method requires its data schema, software revision and assumptions. Reusing an equipment procedure additionally requires calibration, object geometry, admissible operating conditions and an execution monitor. Reusing a scientific conclusion requires evidence about the sampled biological system and measurement process. A skill that retains only successful command text can erase all three applicability boundaries. Model improvement does not repair a missing calibration record or turn an association into a validated mechanism.

The inspected Paper2Agent revision makes a limited verification boundary concrete. Its validate_cases routine can require positive acceptance cases for every expected tool; check_subset compares returned structures with declared expected values; check_artifacts checks returned artifact paths and identity conditions. Those functions support interface and smoke-case checks, not independent validation of a biological interpretation. The source was inspected at revision 8c2d059165ef; no scientific analysis was executed here . Generated tests inherit the assumptions of their expected outputs. An executable wrapper can therefore improve method accessibility while faithfully automating an invalid analysis; interface conformance and scientific validity must remain separate claims.
Figure locates the evidence and execution boundaries in a conceptual scientific-agent loop.

Only records already accepted by the declared verifier enter the current-source validity and publication-authority gates. A released surrogate or replay finding retains its backend and recording provenance; it is not fresh physical evidence. Closing either loop does not identify a causal improvement or establish unrestricted laboratory autonomy.

Cutts and colleagues report three agent-guided aptamer design–test–improve rounds in October 2026 . The myoglobin results in Table are nonmonotonic across rounds. Human researchers performed the laboratory workflow, and the agent platform changed after the first round. The study therefore provides empirical evidence of iterative laboratory feedback and failure diagnosis, while its authors explicitly reserve matched-budget no-feedback and non-reasoning controls for future work. These observations do not isolate the causal contribution of agentic reasoning from harness changes, prior-round seeds or accumulated assay information.

The nonmonotonic middle round is analytically important. Optimizing an assay proxy can concentrate candidates in a region with favorable background interactions rather than the desired biological property. A memory writer that records only the apparent successful motif can promote the shortcut into a procedural prior. A writer that retains target and background evidence, candidate lineage, analysis revision and uncertainty makes the lesson revisable. This is the biological counterpart of a coding agent memorizing a test-specific patch: a higher proxy score can accompany weaker alignment with the actual objective.
For a transparent analysis, consider the illustrative measurement model

Here is candidate in round , the declared assay conditions, its measurement batch, a batch effect, and the observed scalar response; all additive terms have the response’s units. This is an analytical model, not a fitted model of the cited experiment. If candidate strategy changes only between batches, differences in and are not separately identified without additional design or assumptions. Randomized allocation within batches, recurring controls, replicated candidates and independent confirmation can address different parts of that ambiguity. Repeated reads of one construct are measurement replication; they do not create independent evidence about unrelated molecular families.

An agent-design comparison must therefore randomize complete campaigns or sufficiently isolated candidate allocations, preserve assay conditions and measurement budgets, and predeclare which feedback is available before each proposal. Include conventional sequential-design and no-feedback controls, not only a weak language-model prompt. Hold out candidate families or experimental regimes when the claim concerns transfer. Evaluate the selected designs and the learned predictor separately: finding a promising candidate and predicting unseen candidates are different achievements. Costs include physical measurements, waiting, failed jobs, analyst review and computational selection. Token expenditure alone is an inadequate resource boundary when empirical feedback dominates elapsed time.

Autonomous Science Bench, released in October 2026, makes that discovery–learning distinction explicit through two acceptance gates . Version 0.1 contains six campaigns: five return recorded measurements and one uses a hidden surrogate. A live backend and adaptive allocation scheduler are planned, rather than evaluated results in that release. The laboratory service owns the measurement ledger independently of the agent, and grading combines measured-design quality with prediction on held-out designs. These design choices support controlled evaluation of sequential decisions; they do not constitute six live autonomous laboratory demonstrations.

The backend is part of the scientific claim. A replay can provide genuine historical measurements while excluding unrecorded designs. A digital twin permits more queries but tests optimization against its approximation and training coverage. A live assay adds drift, failed measurements, delayed returns and limits on reversibility. An interface that makes those backends look identical to the agent does not make their evidence interchangeable. Report backend provenance with every outcome and measure whether an agent exploits surrogate artifacts that fail under independent measurement.

Biological scope also constrains the autonomy claim. The aptamer study uses non-infectious protein targets under its stated laboratory conditions and does not study clinical efficacy, human subjects, or animal models . An assay hit therefore remains an assay-specific observation. Extending a workflow to a different biological system requires its own material, measurement, containment, and approval conditions; preserving an API schema supplies none of those premises. The relevant system boundary includes the people or equipment that accept a proposed experiment and the independent evidence required before a scientific conclusion is promoted.

Delayed results create a further state boundary. Submitted, measured, quality-controlled and scientifically accepted experiments should have distinct identifiers and statuses. An agent must not treat an unreturned measurement as a negative label or spend the same physical budget twice after a timeout. When a result is corrected, dependent hypotheses and skills become stale without erasing the historical reason for their adoption. These requirements connect biological research to the session journal of Chapter , the conditioning analysis of Chapter and the recovery contracts of Chapter . The cross-domain synthesis concerns preservation of evidence, authority and effect identity; it does not imply that software verifiers and biological assays have equivalent error models.

Enterprise context is governed by principals, groups, purpose, retention, and changing access policy. Retrieval must enforce these constraints at use time. A document indexed while a user had access may become unauthorized later. An embedding or extracted summary can preserve sensitive information after the original file is removed. Therefore permission checks cannot be limited to the connector’s initial ingestion step.

Let a retrieved record carry source identity , subject , validity interval, and authorization epoch . Before the record enters , the application evaluates whether the current principal may use for the requested purpose under the current epoch. A cached positive decision is reusable only within the policy’s declared validity conditions. The record’s textual content cannot grant its own authority. Instructions discovered inside a document remain data unless promoted through an authorized application channel.

Business workflow agents also depend on schema and process state. A customer-service action can be valid for one account tier and invalid for another. A procurement step may require approval after a threshold is crossed. These constraints should be represented in tool preconditions and authoritative business logic. Asking the language model to remember all exceptions from a policy manual creates an avoidable single point of failure.

Platforms such as Agentforce, ServiceNow’s agent tooling, SAP Joule Studio, and Copilot Studio document domain-integrated development surfaces . The transferable technical question is how those surfaces preserve identity and process constraints across model decisions, connectors, and human review. Their domain integration does not establish that every generated action is correct, nor that all deployment configurations enforce the same controls.

A discriminating test changes access or process state midway through a session. The agent previously read a document or prepared an action, then the principal loses access or the business object changes. Evaluate whether retrieval, pending approvals, and queued actions are invalidated appropriately. A successful fresh-session test is insufficient because the failure lives in stale context and in-flight work. Report benign task completion alongside containment to expose overblocking as well as unauthorized use.

A memory engine can store raw events, extract facts, build a graph, summarize experience, or expose reflection operations. These are distinct mechanisms. Storing more information can improve coverage while increasing retrieval noise and governance burden. A graph can encode temporal relationships without guaranteeing that the selected facts remain valid. A reflection operation can produce a useful abstraction or reinforce a mistaken interpretation.

Mem0, Graphiti/Zep, Hindsight, MemOS, and OpenViking expose different storage and context-management surfaces . The comparison should identify the unit written, retrieval policy, update semantics, provenance, deletion propagation, and compatibility with the consuming model. A memory product’s use of the word learning does not establish changes to model parameters. The actual update target must be inspected.

Temporal memory requires both event time and system knowledge time. An event can occur on one date and be discovered later. A correction can invalidate a prior belief without making the historical observation disappear. A system that stores only the most recent text may lose the explanation for past decisions; one that stores every version without validity filtering may repeatedly retrieve obsolete facts. The application must define which temporal question it is answering.

Memory evaluation also needs a no-memory baseline and an oracle-retrieval control. The former reveals negative transfer; the latter separates storage and retrieval limitations from downstream interpretation. Construction cost belongs inside the accounting boundary. A memory engine can reduce per-task prompt size while spending substantial inference on extraction, consolidation, or maintenance. Amortization depends on reuse and should be reported as a function of workload, not assumed from one benchmark.

Licensing and inspectability remain artifact-specific. Where a repository’s license and additional README restrictions appear inconsistent, record the conflict and avoid an unqualified legal classification. The technical consequence is uncertainty about reuse and deployment, not an inference about enforceability. More importantly for scientific comparison, source visibility should not be confused with an audited implementation. A public memory schema can still omit crucial behavior implemented by a remote service.

Table completes the catalog with research, business, vertical, and memory systems. It describes the role established by the inspected resource and the evidence needed before accepting a stronger claim. Product families can overlap; the categories organize experimental questions rather than define exclusive market segments. Names and source redirects are preserved without importing prior rankings or unverified ownership assertions.

The unresolved Qianfan source is included as an identity lead with unknown detailed behavior. This is more informative than silently omitting a regional product or guessing its controls from a neighboring offering. The same principle applies to feature parity across regions, deployment tiers, and private-cloud options: absence of inspected evidence constrains the claim. It does not establish absence of the feature.

Legal and customer-service systems require domain-specific outcomes. A legal workflow should be evaluated for source validity, jurisdiction, document consistency, review burden, and unauthorized disclosure. A support agent should be evaluated for policy compliance, resolution, escalation, and adverse actions, not only conversational satisfaction. A general benchmark can supply useful stress tests, but it cannot substitute for the domain’s operational specification.

Organizational benefit is not directly measured by model benchmark accuracy. An agent can produce useful drafts while increasing review effort, or reduce time on routine work while creating rare costly errors. Deployment studies must define the outcome and the accounting boundary. Candidate outcomes include verified task completion, time to accepted artifact, reviewer effort, rework, error severity, and downstream process effects.

The Knowledge Activation paper proposes structured institutional knowledge units and reports an enterprise case study . Its developer survey supports claims about perceived experience in that setting. Self-reported time savings are not instrumented productivity measurements, and concurrent model or tooling changes complicate causal attribution. The useful architectural contribution can therefore be discussed without promoting the case study into a universal magnitude claim.

A stronger study randomizes eligible work units or uses a carefully justified staggered rollout. The unit of assignment should minimize interference: engineers sharing skills and repositories can transfer treatment effects to nominal controls. Measure baseline workload, task difficulty, and prior tool exposure. Record adoption and noncompliance, because assigning an agent does not guarantee that workers use it. An intention-to-treat analysis and a usage-conditioned analysis answer different questions and should not be conflated.

Learning effects require longitudinal observation. Early users may spend extra time configuring context and tools; later users may benefit from accumulated skills. Conversely, initial novelty can inflate perceived benefit while maintenance costs appear later. Report trajectories rather than only a single post-deployment mean. Include unsuccessful and abandoned tasks, since excluding them can make a system appear faster by conditioning on completion.

External validity depends on organizational knowledge quality. A system grounded in accurate, maintained procedures may perform differently from one grounded in contradictory documentation. The treatment therefore includes knowledge engineering and governance, not merely an agent interface. An ablation can hold the model and harness fixed while varying institutional context quality. This identifies whether observed gains come from the policy, better information, or their interaction.

Professional-task benchmarks attempt to move evaluation beyond short questions into deliverables with multiple constraints. Their relevance is substantial, but the mapping to economic impact requires care. A benchmark task can resemble professional work while omitting coordination, accountability, access friction, and consequences of failure. A successful artifact is evidence about the tested task, not a direct estimate of organizational value or labor substitution.

Agents’ Last Exam introduces long-horizon professional tasks with verifiable outcomes across occupational categories . Its living-benchmark design requires exact task-pool and scoring snapshots for longitudinal comparison. An improved score can reflect a changed task mix or grader as well as a stronger system. Reports should retain the task version, evaluator identity, available tools, and artifact requirements rather than cite a moving leaderboard alone.

Economic interpretation also depends on selection. Benchmarks often choose tasks with accessible data and checkable outcomes. Work requiring tacit negotiation, physical access, or responsibility allocation may be underrepresented. This selection does not invalidate the benchmark; it limits the population to which results generalize. A transparent survey should state which professional activities the evaluation captures and which remain outside its observation boundary.

Task cost must include verification and remediation. Let gross production benefit be , execution cost , review cost , and expected failure loss . A deployment decision depends on under a specified workload. These quantities may be uncertain and correlated. Faster generation can increase review volume, while stronger checks can reduce failure loss at additional cost. No universal conversion from token throughput to economic value follows.

The proposed evaluation therefore combines benchmark tasks with deployment-specific shadow runs. Shadow execution observes what the agent would propose without granting consequential effects. It can reveal permission and evidence failures while preserving a human-controlled process. It does not fully measure autonomous deployment because humans and environments may behave differently when the agent’s actions are real. The limitation should remain explicit when interpreting readiness.

A research agent can implement evidence review as a transaction over claim records. New sources enter a staging area, identity resolution determines lineage and version, extraction proposes claims, and validation checks support and conflicts. Only then are accepted claims available for synthesis. Rejected or unresolved claims remain auditable without becoming authoritative memory. This separates acquisition success from evidential acceptance.

The identity binds the source lineage and inspected version; every observation in retains its location. Each records a proposition, applicable population, evidence class, source version, locator, assumptions, and unresolved limitations. Proposal does not imply support. Let be the declared, versioned evidence corpus accessible under current research authorization; it may include relevant sources beyond the current extraction and staged records. For ,

The operator retrieves relevant disagreements from , the current located evidence, and prior staged records, retaining source identities and locators. The audit returns a verdict and its evidence ; the values denote rejected, unresolved, and accepted. The record states which scope or evidence-class check failed. The append operator preserves each review occurrence, including rejected and unresolved records, without silently deduplicating their audit history.

Acceptance is versioned evidence, not a permanent property of a proposition. Let indicate that record has no unresolved invalidation under the current source versions, declared research scope, and review procedure. Here extracts the recorded verdict, not an assertion of objective truth; the subscript on makes the view time-dependent even when the append-only ledger is unchanged. The complete ledger remains available to authorized audit even when a record is absent from the synthesis view. A failed freshness check quarantines the dependent inference until re-review; it need not erase the observation that originally supported it. No candidate becomes authoritative merely because extraction or proposal succeeded. The audit function is not assumed infallible. It can combine deterministic checks, independent model review, and human adjudication, each with measured error characteristics. A deterministic check can verify that a cited page exists, but not that it supports an inference. A second model can detect some mismatches while sharing the first model’s biases. Human review can resolve ambiguity but introduces cost and variation. The implementation should record which evidence supported acceptance.

This transaction is particularly valuable when the research output becomes enterprise memory. Without staging, a speculative conclusion can be consolidated into a reusable skill and later appear as established policy. Requiring an evidence class and validity scope makes that promotion visible. Subsequent corrections can invalidate dependent records and trigger reevaluation of artifacts that used them. The system still needs a retention policy for sensitive source material and an authorization check before reuse.

Evaluation should seed incorrect citations, outdated versions, incompatible populations, and plausible unsupported conclusions. Also include valid minority findings that conflict with a popular narrative. Measure support precision, coverage of decisive evidence, conflict retention, abstention, and revision correctness. These metrics prevent the system from optimizing citation count or agreement at the expense of scientific accuracy. They also provide a concrete basis for comparing research products whose internal architecture is unavailable.

Consider an enterprise research agent preparing an internal recommendation about a vendor. It retrieves a pricing document, a legal assessment, and an operational incident note. The documents have different owners and access scopes. During the task, the legal assessment is corrected and the requesting employee changes teams, losing access to part of the workspace. The agent’s active context still contains the earlier excerpts. A fresh retrieval permission check alone cannot remove those excerpts from the current computation or from previously generated summaries.

The first design requirement is dependency tracking. Every extracted claim and generated summary should identify the source versions it used. When the legal assessment changes, the system marks dependent claims stale and prevents them from being promoted as current evidence. This does not imply that all prior artifacts must be automatically deleted: some may be retained as historical records under appropriate access controls. The key distinction is between historical provenance and current applicability.

The second requirement is authority revalidation. A pending action to share the recommendation must be checked under the employee’s current principal and purpose. Historical access does not authorize a new disclosure. If the current context contains content no longer permitted for the intended action, the application can rebuild a restricted context or require a controlled review path. It should not ask the model to infer access from the prose, because the decisive policy state may be absent or deliberately untrusted.

The third requirement is correction propagation. Updating the original document and vector index does not update a separately stored summary, a procedural note, or another agent’s copied context. A dependency graph can enumerate these derivatives, but actual propagation may be asynchronous. The service should expose whether invalidation is pending, complete, or impossible for a particular external copy. A claim of immediate deletion across all surfaces would require evidence about those surfaces, not simply successful deletion of one database row.

A useful experiment stages the policy change at several points: before retrieval, after retrieval but before synthesis, after synthesis but before sharing, and after a recipient has accessed the artifact. The expected control differs at each stage. Before sharing, the system can block or regenerate. After disclosure, it may revoke further access but cannot guarantee that the recipient forgot or did not copy the information. Recovery metrics should reflect this irreversibility instead of treating every revocation as full restoration.

The comparison conditions should include connector-only checks, retrieval-time checks, and dependency-aware checks spanning derived memory and artifact publication. Hold the model and documents fixed. Measure unauthorized disclosure, use of stale claims, valid recommendation quality, review burden, and completion latency. A system that blocks every recommendation after any policy change has strong containment but poor utility; a system that always completes may have the opposite profile. Reporting both axes prevents a degenerate policy from appearing universally superior.

This case also clarifies why enterprise deployment evidence cannot be borrowed from a generic question-answering benchmark. The difficult behavior is not recalling a sentence but maintaining a coherent relationship among evidence version, principal, purpose, and action time. A memory engine can improve retrieval while leaving that relationship unenforced. A workflow platform can enforce approvals while presenting stale evidence to reviewers. A model can reason correctly about the visible documents while lacking the current policy state. The system must join these layers explicitly.

For implementation, represent each artifact with a content digest, source-version dependencies, audience, purpose, and approval record. Store access decisions separately from the artifact text so they can expire or be revoked. Generate the model-visible authority summary from current policy, and record the epoch used at each effect boundary. These are concrete engineering requirements that can be checked without claiming that the model has a complete understanding of organizational intent. The remaining semantic judgment concerns whether the recommendation follows from the authorized, current evidence; that judgment still needs a calibrated evaluator and appropriate review.

The evaluator should also inspect who could observe each intermediate artifact. A final recommendation may be properly restricted while a temporary spreadsheet or trace exposes the underlying assessment to a broader audience. Thus the privacy unit is the complete artifact lineage, not merely the final answer. Instrumented tests can enumerate created objects and compare their access policies with the task contract. Where an application does not expose intermediate-object visibility, the corresponding claim remains unverified. This is a concrete observation limit and should affect the deployment assurance case rather than be replaced by a general statement that the platform is secure.

An executable evaluator can be wrong about what it certifies. TestJack’s October 2026 witness construction targets candidates that pass existing tests while violating prompt-grounded requirements . The resulting conflict is between an operational gate and a task property; it is not resolved by declaring either a test or a language-model reviewer an oracle. This current case motivates the chapter’s separation of internal interventions, executable verification, evaluator classification error, and release evidence.

Inspection asks what a model or execution system is doing. Verification asks whether a specified property holds under declared assumptions. The two can support one another, but neither subsumes the other. An interpretable activation pattern does not prove that a tool action is authorized. A passing test does not reveal the complete internal mechanism that produced the artifact. A reliable technical account must identify the property, observation boundary, intervention, and residual uncertainty for each claim.

This chapter connects internal model interventions to executable task validators and evidence-based quality gates. It emphasizes false acceptance, evaluator dependence, and specification gaps because these are the points where apparent assurance can exceed actual support. Every proposed test remains a proposed experiment unless execution evidence is available.

Start with a property of artifact or action in environment . A verifier observes a projection and returns accept, reject, or unresolved. The projection can omit decisive state. For example, a screenshot may not show a file’s location, and a test log may not identify the artifact revision. No verifier can reliably recover distinctions absent from its observation without additional assumptions or queries.

This leads to three separate questions. Is the property well defined? Does the observation contain evidence sufficient to judge it? Does the verifier use that evidence correctly? A weak result at the third stage can be improved by a stronger judge. A failure at the second stage requires a better observation interface. A failure at the first stage requires specification or adjudication, not merely more inference. Collapsing these cases into one accuracy score obscures the intervention needed.

Formal verification supplies strong conclusions when the model, specification, and proof obligations are appropriate. Its guarantee remains conditional on those objects representing the deployed system. A proof about a pure function does not establish the behavior of a surrounding agent that calls another version, supplies invalid inputs, or operates with changed permissions. The deployment boundary must bind the verified artifact and assumptions to actual execution.

Executable tests provide finite observations. They can falsify a candidate under the tested conditions and can estimate behavior over a sampled distribution. Passing them does not prove a universal property. Nonetheless, a reproducible failing test is stronger evidence than an unsupported critique because another investigator can replay the witness. The key is to preserve the relationship between the witness and the intended requirement rather than accept every disagreement with a reference implementation as a defect.

An assurance case organizes these distinctions. Its claims identify required properties; evidence records observations and proofs; arguments explain why the evidence supports the claims; defeaters identify conditions that invalidate the argument. This structure is especially valuable for agents because the system changes across sessions, memory updates, model releases, and tool schemas. Assurance must track those dependencies instead of treating one successful evaluation as permanent certification.
For a binary property and a fixed observation , let . Under zero–one loss, the minimum error over all measurable classifiers using only is

At each observation, choosing the more probable class minimizes conditional error; averaging gives the expression. It is a population identity, not an estimate available without labeled data. Two equally probable states with identical observations and opposite property values contribute an irreducible error of one half on that ambiguous subset. More inference over the same evidence cannot remove the ambiguity. Additional authoritative queries can change and therefore change the bound; a richer explanation generated from the original cannot add independent evidence. This supplies a formal reason to diagnose observation loss separately from judge weakness.

Activation inspection begins by recording internal states associated with particular inputs and outputs. A probe can predict a property from an activation without showing that the model uses that property to decide. Correlation can arise because the activation reflects another variable or because the probe extracts information unavailable to the model’s downstream computation. Causal claims require interventions and carefully stated counterfactuals.

Activation patching typically compares a clean input, a corrupted input, and a corrupted computation in which selected activations are restored from the clean run. The measured recovery depends on what was corrupted, which sites were patched, and which output metric was used. A patch can have a large effect because it repairs many entangled variables rather than a uniquely interpretable concept. The intervention distribution is therefore part of the claim.

As a methodological foundation, Meng and colleagues’ 2022 work uses causal tracing to investigate factual associations and test rank-one model editing through ROME . The important evidence connects localized interventions to measured changes in factual predictions and editing behavior. It does not establish that every fact occupies one isolated location or that editing a weight removes all related knowledge. The result is bounded by model family, prompts, corruption procedure, and evaluation of specificity and generalization.

Zhang and Nanda’s 2023 methodological study shows that activation-patching conclusions can change with metrics and corruption methods . This is a methodological constraint on interpretation: a heatmap is not a mechanism by itself. A convincing study repeats the analysis under justified alternatives, includes negative controls, and reports which conclusions remain stable. If localization shifts dramatically, the appropriate conclusion is sensitivity to the intervention setup, not a precise biological analogy.

The implementation ledger should identify the activation hooks, cached tensors, patch function, corrupted-input constructor, and metric computation. Verify tensor shapes and token positions; a shifted position can patch the wrong event while producing plausible visual output. Then compare no-patch, random-site patch, targeted patch, and relevant ablations. Model outputs should be evaluated on held-out prompts, including cases where the proposed concept is absent or ambiguous. These controls constrain causal interpretation without pretending to reveal the entire model.

A compatible confidence sequence can accommodate repeated looks; searching many explanations additionally requires multiplicity control. This estimates the declared intervention average. It does not identify a uniquely correct circuit or certify that the score captures mechanistic truth. Clipping an unbounded recovery score changes the estimand and must be disclosed.
The sampling path and the evidence-acquisition path impose different identification conditions (Figure ).

Verification depends on evidence and inference. The upper is a specified latent property; the lower is a declared intervention score. Additional queries can change observability. Only samples ; both densities are evaluated at that sample to form . Target support and bounded predictable weights are assumptions. An interval for the resulting estimand does not establish mechanistic truth.

Sparse autoencoders approximate an activation vector using a small number of learned dictionary features. A common objective combines reconstruction error with a sparsity constraint or penalty. Let be a model activation, sparse feature activations, and a decoder dictionary. The reconstruction term measures approximation in activation space. It does not directly measure whether feature labels are correct or whether all behaviorally important structure is represented.

Anthropic’s 2023 monosemanticity report applies dictionary learning to a small transformer and analyzes feature interpretation, intervention, splitting, and limitations . OpenAI’s 2024 sparse-autoencoder work studies scalable training and evaluation of reconstruction, sparsity, and feature quality . These are primary research contributions with different scopes. Neither establishes that a sparse representation is a unique, complete ontology of the model’s concepts.

Feature interpretation must examine more than maximally activating examples. A feature can look clean at its strongest activations while responding to unrelated contexts at lower levels. Sampling only impressive examples introduces selection bias. Evaluation should include activation ranges, random examples, counterexamples, and downstream interventions. Automatic feature descriptions generated by another model require independent checking; a fluent label can rationalize a mixed feature.

Reconstruction and causal faithfulness can diverge. A dictionary can reconstruct common activation patterns well while missing rare behavior that matters for security or authorization. Conversely, a feature intervention can change behavior by moving computation off the model’s natural activation manifold. The resulting effect is evidence about that intervention, not necessarily evidence that the feature normally causes the behavior in the same way.

For agent inspection, the relevant question is whether a feature-level explanation improves a concrete decision or detects a failure under held-out conditions. Compare it with simpler probes, input-output monitors, and executable checks at matched access and cost. A feature-based monitor should be tested after model updates, context compaction, and tool changes because its calibration may depend on the original distribution. Internal access can provide useful evidence while remaining an additional system component with its own drift and false-alarm behavior.

The preceding circuit and dictionary methods are methodological foundations, not descriptions of the entire October 2026 inspection frontier. Contemporary oversight also uses monitors of reasoning traces, actions and tool results. These observations are complementary to internal activations: a readable trace is neither a complete causal account nor a proof that an accepted action satisfies its specification.

The August implicit-influence study compares matched nudges delivered as incidental contextual details or as explicit instructions to use and conceal the nudge . Across its tested task formats and extended-thinking models, behavioral influence can persist while trace-based detection weakens substantially in the implicit condition. Consequently, a monitor validated mainly on explicit concealment instructions can face a different observation problem in ordinary biased decision making. Its GPT-5-based judge does not establish that the influence is undetectable in principle; for Claude 4.5 runs the observed channel is an API summary rather than raw thinking. These are material access limits, not evidence that all reasoning traces are uninformative.

OpenAI’s April 2026 release supplies datasets and metric code, but explicitly describes its public evaluation scaffold as illustrative and mocked, omitting restricted environments . The inspected gmean_minimal_criterion routine computes an effect-normalized detection bound with eligibility conditions; bootstrapped_gmean_metric separates eligibility selection from estimation and resamples within instance–arm strata. Its reported quantity must not be relabeled ordinary classifier accuracy or a direct measurement of complete causal faithfulness. Report the eligible-instance fraction alongside the conditional metric; an undefined case is not evidence of zero monitor error. The source revision is d14f181a0623; it was inspected, not executed .

The September Astra system card supplies an additional current boundary: it distinguishes CoT-only, action-only and full-context monitors and reports reduced CoT monitorability relative to earlier models on its evaluations . These are provider-reported configured results. Full-context access contains evidence absent from a trace-only monitor, so a comparison must hold observation scope fixed before attributing a difference to the monitor model. The existence of a full-context deployment monitor does not establish the same visibility for an application consuming an ordinary API response or a summarized reasoning field.

A discriminating experiment crosses actor checkpoint, monitor checkpoint, observation scope, context transformation and adversarial awareness. Freeze complete trajectories for the monitor comparison; separately rerun actors when studying how awareness changes behavior. Compressing a trajectory after the fact measures evidence loss to the monitor, whereas letting the actor reason under compacted context changes both behavior and available evidence. Preserve that distinction when interpreting the interaction. Evaluate sensitivity to implicit influence, false alarms on benign reasoning, alert delay relative to effect commitment, and compute cost. A monitor that identifies an error after an irreversible effect provides diagnostic evidence but has not demonstrated preventive control. An internal signal should become a deployment gate only after its held-out calibration and intervention consequences have been tested at the actual action boundary.
