The next-task distribution is unknown. Estimating it from recent tasks favors recency; estimating it from all history favors retention. Neither choice guarantees that a rare future instruction survives. A practical system can retain raw evidence under its retention policy while maintaining a smaller derived index, but archival retention and usable retrieval remain separate properties. Immutability of an audit record is not permission to retain prohibited content indefinitely.

Forgetting also requires a distinction between utility pruning and revocation. A low-utility procedure may remain authorized but rarely relevant. A revoked credential or instruction must cease to influence execution even if it would improve task success. A memory optimizer that removes entries only according to observed reward cannot implement that requirement. Authorization metadata must constrain reads, derived summaries, cached contexts, and reconstructed skills across concurrent sessions.

Feedback provenance is equally important. A skill extracted from a trajectory judged successful may encode a workaround that bypassed the intended requirement. Store the tested outcome and its verifier scope, not an unqualified assertion that the procedure is correct. When later evidence contradicts the procedure, the update should preserve the conflict and the affected dependency closure rather than silently overwrite history. Continual adaptation needs a mechanism for learning that an earlier lesson was wrong.

An improver evaluation starts multiple independent improvement runs from the same initial executor. It varies only the improver, allocates the same search budget, and evaluates resulting executors on untouched external tasks. The outcomes include final held-out quality, quality as a function of consumed resources, regression severity, diversity of changes, and the frequency of invalid or unsafe proposals. A single successful search trajectory cannot estimate the distribution of improver performance.

AIDE2 explicitly distinguishes this issue through its ignition test. Its discovered research agent is used as an outer-loop improver and compared with a human-engineered improver, holding the initial inner-loop agent fixed. The paper reports three seeds per arm and concludes that the evidence is inconclusive about superior self-improvement efficiency. This limitation is central: improved research execution does not by itself show that improvement will accelerate when the agent becomes its own optimizer .

An original discriminating protocol is the following. Pre-register two improvers, fixed executor initialization, a search task stream, independent validation tasks, and a sealed final evaluation population. Randomize search seeds and task orders. Count proposal generation, failed executions, verifier calls, environment setup, memory maintenance, and selection cost. At predetermined resource checkpoints, freeze the incumbent executor and evaluate it without feeding results back into search. Compare complete cost-quality curves rather than only each run’s selected maximum.

This indexed family retains distinct run and checkpoint identities even when their executor snapshots are equal. The formulation separates selection feedback from assessment of the improver. In practice, evaluator isolation requires access control and logging. If an agent can inspect hidden tests, final benchmark files, or previous final-evaluation outputs through a shared workspace, the separation has failed. Improving a scoring script can be legitimate when the script is wrong, but that intervention must be reported and evaluated as a change in the measurement system.

Repeated improvement creates two kinds of accumulated state: executable changes and beliefs about why those changes help. Both need rollback. An acceptance record should include the hypothesis, modified artifacts, compatibility tuple, validation outcomes, held-out outcomes, resource cost, known regressions, and the exact conditions for reversal. Returning to old code while retaining a newly trained model or incompatible memory does not restore the old system.

Deployment should be gated on the property being changed. A context-saving edit needs tests for rare decision-critical information and conditioning consistency. A skill update needs applicability and permission checks. A learned router needs no-valid-tool and schema-drift tests. A verifier update needs independent adversarial cases. A model update needs behavioral and memory-interpretation regression tests. A global score can supplement these checks but cannot replace them, because many failures occupy a small probability mass with high consequence.

The strongest current evidence supports bounded adaptation mechanisms under specified task and feedback conditions. The harder open problem is maintaining trustworthy selection as executor capability, evaluator behavior, state representations, and environments co-evolve. A system that becomes increasingly effective at satisfying a fixed evaluator may be improving the intended task, exploiting the evaluator, or both. The decisive evidence comes from independent transfer, mechanism ablations, preserved failure records, and explicit evaluation of the improvement process itself.

Agentic serving is a workload of correlated model calls separated by tools, waiting, branching, and state updates. The prompt of the next call often overlaps a prior prompt, but its useful overlap depends on serialization, context editing, and model compatibility. A tool can pause generation long enough for a cache to be evicted; several workers can share an initial prefix and then diverge; a resumed session can return to another serving replica. A benchmark that repeatedly decodes independent fixed-length prompts misses these interactions.

Represent a session by turns , each with input length , generated length , reused prefix length , tool duration , and state-transform identifier . For serial calls whose tool waits do not overlap model work, elapsed time is

where includes admission and scheduling delay. This equality is an accounting identity for that serial workload. Speculative tool execution, parallel workers, and overlapping serving stages require a dependency graph whose critical path replaces the sum; adding overlapping durations would double-count time. Reporting model time alone omits delays that often determine whether an agent finishes within its deadline.

The September 2026 vLLM AgentX engineering account explicitly treats multi-turn agent traffic, prefix reuse, scheduling, and prefill/decode disaggregation as a coupled serving problem. Its reported throughput and cost comparisons are configuration- and workload-dependent vendor evidence. They cannot be transferred to arbitrary task completion or substituted for quality-matched end-to-end measurements . The analysis below therefore derives resource constraints under explicit hypothetical assumptions and identifies what a measurement must establish.

The serving policy itself can affect reasoning and memory behavior. Aggressive truncation changes observations. A timeout can cause the harness to retry and consume a different random continuation. Admission control can alter which parallel branch finishes first and therefore which evidence a selector sees. These are changes in the executed policy, even when the model weights are fixed. Performance optimization should preserve the declared behavioral contract or measure the consequences of changing it.

Batching trades weight amortization against KV traffic and latency. Increasing reduces weight bytes per output token but increases total state and can delay individual sequences. A scheduler optimized for aggregate tokens per second can worsen the time until a particular tool call is issued. For agents whose next action unlocks external work, the cost of that delay can propagate through an entire workflow. Performance should therefore include per-session interactivity and task-critical latency, not only engine utilization.

Cache reuse requires a compatibility predicate. At minimum, relevant tokens, model and adapter weights, positions, attention masks, architecture mode, and numerical representation must agree with the cached computation. The causal dependency graph matters: editing an earlier token changes later hidden states, so suffix KV values are not generally reusable merely because their token strings are unchanged. A semantic embedding similarity score cannot certify equality of those tensors.

For a sequence of causal transformer layers, the invalidation rule follows by induction. A changed input embedding at position changes that position’s hidden state. At the next attention layer, every later position whose receptive field includes may change. Those changes propagate through residual and feed-forward transformations and into later-layer keys and values. Local or sliding-window attention can bound some dependency paths, but hybrid full-attention layers may restore long-range dependence. Exact invalidation must use the actual architecture, not the visual location of a changed text span.

The inspected vLLM V1 module vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py exposes distinct methods for computed-block lookup, slot allocation, cache reset, and computed-block truncation. Those control points make it possible to audit whether a context transform invalidates the dependent state before reuse. They are implementation interfaces, not a proof that a particular deployment invokes them correctly . A cache test should alter one dependency at a time: adapter identity, position offset, prefix token, mask, or tool-result serialization, then compare with a fresh computation within declared precision tolerances.

A reusable key should identify computation, tenancy, and policy constraints. Hashing only token content risks collisions across incompatible adapters or security domains. Tenant isolation can require separate namespaces even when two prompts contain identical public text. A deletion request may also require removal from derived cache tiers, or at least prevention of future reads according to the declared policy. The mathematical possibility of reuse does not imply permission to reuse.

The September 2026 tiered-offloading design places host memory between accelerator storage and secondary tiers such as filesystems, object stores, and remote peers. Reload and offload have different allocation and synchronization costs . A useful admission criterion compares reuse probability and avoided recomputation with transfer and occupancy costs:

Every term must use consistent units, such as dollars or time-weighted utility. A byte hit rate alone cannot establish net benefit when lookup delays block a critical request or when retained state displaces more valuable work.

Weight quantization, activation quantization, and KV quantization change different error pathways. GPTQ targets post-training weight approximation, while SmoothQuant redistributes activation difficulty to make low-precision execution more practical . Their historical methods remain useful foundations; the current implementation choice must be checked against the target architecture, kernels, and 2026 model release. A nominal bit width is not a complete specification: group size, scales, accumulation precision, outlier handling, and supported matrix shapes affect both numerical behavior and performance.

For an agent, a small logit perturbation can cause a discrete tool change. Average text perplexity is therefore an incomplete acceptance metric. Evaluate schema validity, tool selection, argument fidelity, termination, rare constraints, and task success. If the top two action probabilities are close, a modest numerical change can reverse their ordering even when most token probabilities are nearly unchanged. A quality-preserving quantization claim needs the decision distribution and workload that matter to the application.

Speculative decoding proposes tokens with a draft mechanism and verifies them with the target model. Under the appropriate acceptance rule, the goal is to preserve the target sampling distribution while reducing costly sequential target work . Its benefit depends on acceptance, verification cost, draft cost, batch interaction, and available hardware parallelism. A high acceptance rate does not guarantee a speedup if the draft consumes the same bottleneck resource or increases memory pressure enough to reduce concurrency.

For independent identically distributed cycles with finite mean duration and positive finite mean progress, the ratio of those means is the long-run time per emitted token by renewal-reward accounting. It is neither the expectation of each cycle’s time/progress ratio nor a latency percentile. Adaptive cycles, shared-resource contention, and changing context lengths require a justified stationary model or direct measurement. Structured tool outputs create additional boundaries. Drafted tokens cannot trigger side effects before the target output, parser, authorization policy, and commit logic accept the action. Streaming a plausible partial tool call into execution defeats the intended separation between speculative text and committed behavior.

The 2026 Speculate with Memory method retains transition statistics, retrieved episodes, and recurring prediction errors in a speculator while leaving the actor’s context unchanged. It predicts actions, observations, or chains during available computation windows and checks exact matches before reusing speculative work. Its prelaunch restriction excludes irreversible writes. The distinction from token-level speculative decoding is essential: a prediction can launch an environment query or an actor call, not merely propose the next token. Reported match accuracy and theoretical latency savings are not identical to end-to-end deployment speedups .

Shared accelerator contention, extra API requests, and coordination can further reduce the realized benefit. A memory ablation must therefore measure both match quality and the critical-path cost of obtaining that quality.

Functional equivalence also requires more than identical action type and arguments. A read-only query issued early may observe a different version of a changing environment. Reusing its response later can alter the actor’s context even though no irreversible write occurred. Exact trajectory preservation requires an appropriate snapshot, stable observation semantics, or freshness validation. Prelaunch can also consume rate limits or expose data to an additional service. The claim is consequently conditional on the workload’s effect, time, authority, and resource contracts, not an unrestricted property of every operation labeled read-only.
